title.zh: 卷一百七十三 列傳第六十: 崔斌 崔彧 葉李 燕公楠 馬紹
title.en: Volume 173 Biographies 60: Cui Bin, Cui Yu, Ye Li, Yan Gongnan, Ma Shao
title.raw: 卷一百七十三 列傳第六十: 崔斌 崔彧 葉李 燕公楠 馬紹 Volume 173 Biographies 60: Cui Bin, Cui Yu, Ye Li, Yan Gongnan, Ma Shao

sentences.zh: 崔斌，字仲文，馬邑人。

translations.literal: Cui Bin, style name Zhongwen, was a man of Mayi.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Bin, whose courtesy name was Zhongwen, came from Mayi.

sentences.zh: 性警敏，多智慮，魁岸雄偉，善騎射，尤攻文學，而達政術。

translations.literal: By nature he was alert and keen, full of schemes and plans, tall and imposing in build, skilled at mounted archery, and especially devoted to letters, while also versed in the arts of government.
translations.idiomatic: He was quick-witted and resourceful, with a towering, imposing frame, skilled in horsemanship and archery, deeply versed in literature, and thoroughly capable in statecraft.

sentences.zh: 世祖在潛邸召見，應對稱旨，命佐卜憐吉帶，將游騎戍淮南。

translations.literal: When the Founder was still in his princely residence he summoned him for an audience; his replies pleased the ruler, and he was ordered to assist Bolinjigit in leading light cavalry to garrison Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai Khan summoned him while still heir apparent; Bin answered to his satisfaction and was assigned to assist Bolinjigit in commanding scouting cavalry on garrison duty in Huainan.

sentences.zh: 斌負才略，卜憐吉帶甚敬禮之。

translations.literal: Bin possessed talent and stratagem, and Bolinjigit treated him with great respect.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was gifted with talent and strategic insight, and Bolinjigit held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 兵駐揚州西城，俾斌領騎兵覘敵形勢，斌視敵兵亂，潛出襲之，多所殺獲。

translations.literal: When the army encamped at the western wall of Yangzhou, Bin was made to lead cavalry to reconnoiter the enemy's dispositions; seeing the enemy troops in disorder, he stole out and attacked them, killing and capturing many.
translations.idiomatic: The army was posted at Yangzhou's western ramparts, and Bin was sent with cavalry to scout the enemy. Seeing their ranks in disarray, he made a stealthy sortie, killing and capturing a great many.

sentences.zh: 俄丁父憂，襲授金符，為總管。

translations.literal: Before long he entered mourning for his father, inherited appointment to a gold tally, and became a zongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward his father died; he inherited his father's gold tally and was appointed regional commander.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，改西京參議宣慰司事。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Zhongtong era he was transferred to serve as a deliberative officer of the Xijing Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In 1260 he was reassigned as deliberative officer on the Western Capital Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘗命安童舉漢人識治體者一人，安童舉斌。

translations.literal: The Founder once ordered Antong to recommend one Han man who understood the essentials of governance, and Antong recommended Bin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once told Antong to nominate a Han official who grasped the fundamentals of governance; Antong put forward Bin.

sentences.zh: 入見，敷陳時政得失，曲中宸慮。

translations.literal: On entering audience he laid out the gains and losses of current policy, striking straight to the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: When he was received in audience, he set forth the strengths and failings of current policy in terms that matched the emperor's own concerns.

sentences.zh: 時世祖銳意圖治，斌危言讜論，直指面斥，是非立判，無有所諱。

translations.literal: At that time the Founder was keen to bring order to the realm; Bin spoke stern truths and forthright counsel, pointing straight at faults and rebuking them to the face, right and wrong decided on the spot, with nothing held back.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then intent on reforming government, and Bin spoke blunt, honest counsel—calling out wrongdoing face to face, settling right and wrong on the spot, and holding nothing back.

sentences.zh: 帝幸上都，嘗召斌，斌下馬步從。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Shangdu he once summoned Bin, and Bin dismounted and walked in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: On one visit to Shangdu the emperor summoned Bin, who dismounted and walked beside the imperial procession.

sentences.zh: 帝命之騎，因問為治大體，今當何先。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him to mount, and then asked what the great principles of governance were and what should come first now.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told him to remount and asked what the overarching principles of rule were and what ought to come first.

sentences.zh: 斌以任相對。

translations.literal: Bin answered that it lay in appointing a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Bin replied that the first priority was to appoint the right chief minister.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「汝其為我舉可為相者。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Then recommend someone fit to serve as chief minister for me."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Then name someone you consider fit to serve as chief minister."

sentences.zh: 斌以安童、史天澤對，帝默然良久。

translations.literal: Bin named Antong and Shi Tianze; the emperor was silent for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: Bin named Antong and Shi Tianze; the emperor fell silent for a long interval.

sentences.zh: 斌曰：「陛下豈以臣猥鄙，所舉未允公議，有所惑歟？

translations.literal: Bin said, "Does Your Majesty perhaps think this humble and mean subject's recommendations fail to satisfy public opinion and therefore remain in doubt?
translations.idiomatic: Bin said, "Does Your Majesty perhaps doubt my nominees because I am unworthy, and because the court has not yet endorsed them?

sentences.zh: 今近臣咸在，乞採輿言，陛下裁之。」

translations.literal: All the close attendants are here now; I beg that public opinion be gathered and Your Majesty decide."
translations.idiomatic: All those close at hand are present; I ask that Your Majesty take counsel from them and decide."

sentences.zh: 帝俞其請，斌立馬揚言曰：「有旨問安童為相，可否？」

translations.literal: The emperor approved his request, and Bin, still on horseback, proclaimed aloud, "By imperial order: is Antong fit to serve as chief minister, yes or no?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed; still mounted, Bin called out, "By imperial command: is Antong fit to serve as chief minister—yes or no?"

sentences.zh: 眾歡然呼萬歲。

translations.literal: The assembly joyfully shouted "Long live the emperor!"
translations.idiomatic: The crowd answered with a joyous cry of "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 帝悅，遂以二人並為相。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and thereupon appointed both men as chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, the emperor appointed both men chief ministers at once.

sentences.zh: 除斌左右司郎中。

translations.literal: Bin was appointed Langzhong of the Left and Right Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was appointed director in the Left and Right Secretariat offices.

sentences.zh: 每論事帝前，群言終日不決者，斌以數言決之。

translations.literal: Whenever matters were debated before the emperor and the multitude of opinions could not be settled in a whole day, Bin would settle them in a few words.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever councilors debated before the throne all day without reaching a decision, a few words from Bin would settle the matter.

sentences.zh: 進見，必與近臣偕，其所獻替，雖密近之臣，有不得與聞者，以此人多忌之。

translations.literal: Whenever he came into audience he always went with close attendants, yet what he offered in counsel—even intimate attendants—some could not hear, and for this reason many came to resent him.
translations.idiomatic: He always attended audience alongside the emperor's inner circle, yet counsel he offered was sometimes withheld even from those closest to the throne, and many grew jealous of him for it.

sentences.zh: 會阿合馬立制國用使司，專總財賦，一以掊克為事，斌曰：「與其有聚斂之臣，寧有盜臣！」

translations.literal: When Ahmad established the Bureau for Regulating State Revenue to monopolize finances and made extortion his sole business, Bin said, "Better to have a thief as minister than a minister who amasses wealth by squeezing the people!"
translations.idiomatic: When Ahmad set up the Bureau for Regulating State Revenue to control all finances and devoted himself wholly to squeezing the people, Bin said, "Better a thief in office than a minister who lives by plundering the realm!"

sentences.zh: 於帝前屢斥其奸惡。

translations.literal: Before the emperor he repeatedly denounced Ahmad's treachery and wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: He denounced Ahmad's corruption again and again before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 至元四年，出守東平。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of the Zhiyuan era he went out to guard Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: In 1267 he was sent out to serve as prefect of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 五年，大兵南征，道壽張。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the great army marched south on campaign and passed through Shouzhang.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, as the main army marched south, it passed through Shouzhang.

sentences.zh: 卒有撤民席，投其赤子於地以死，訴于斌。

translations.literal: Some soldiers tore up a civilian's mat and threw his infant to the ground to its death; the man appealed to Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Some soldiers ripped up a villager's sleeping mat and dashed his infant to the ground, killing it; the man brought the case to Bin.

sentences.zh: 斌馳謂主將曰：「未至敵境，而先殺吾民，國有常刑，汝亦當坐。」

translations.literal: Bin galloped to the commanding general and said, "Before we have even reached enemy territory you are already killing our people; the state has fixed penalties, and you too should be punished."
translations.idiomatic: Bin rode at once to the commander and said, "We have not yet reached the enemy, yet you are already killing our own people. The law has fixed penalties for this—you are answerable as well."

sentences.zh: 於是下其卒於獄，自是莫敢犯。

translations.literal: Thereupon those soldiers were put in prison, and from then on none dared to offend.
translations.idiomatic: The men were thrown into prison, and from that day no one dared molest the populace.

sentences.zh: 歲大昆，徵賦如常年，斌馳奏以免，復請於朝，得楮幣十萬緡，以賑民飢。

translations.literal: That year locusts swarmed in great numbers and levies were exacted as in normal years; Bin sent a rapid memorial to secure exemption, then petitioned the court again and obtained one hundred thousand strings of paper currency to relieve the people's famine.
translations.idiomatic: Locusts ravaged the land that year, yet taxes were still levied as usual; Bin sent an urgent memorial to secure exemption, then won from court one hundred thousand strings of paper money to relieve famine among the people.

sentences.zh: 六年，除同僉樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed Associate Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1269 he was made associate administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 襄樊之役，命斌僉河南行省事。

translations.literal: During the Xiangyang–Fancheng campaign he was ordered to serve concurrently on the Henan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: During the siege of Xiangyang and Fancheng he was assigned concurrent duty on the Henan Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 方議攻鹿門山，斌曰：「自峴山西抵萬山，北抵漢江，築城浚塹，以絕餉援，則襄陽可坐制矣。」

translations.literal: Just as they were debating an assault on Mount Lumen, Bin said, "From Mount Xian west to Mount Wan, north to the Han River—if we build fortifications and dig moats to cut off supplies and reinforcements, Xiangyang can be taken without a fight."
translations.idiomatic: While commanders debated storming Mount Lumen, Bin said, "From Mount Xian west to Mount Wan and north to the Han, if we build walls and trenches to sever supply lines, Xiangyang can be brought to heel without a pitched battle."

sentences.zh: 時調曹、濮民丁，屯田南陽。

translations.literal: At that time corvée laborers from Cao and Pu were levied to open garrison farms at Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the time corvée laborers from Cao and Pu were being conscripted for garrison farming around Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 斌議罷曹、濮屯民，以近地兵多者補之，民以為便。

translations.literal: Bin proposed abolishing the Cao and Pu garrison colonists and replacing them with troops from nearby districts that had surplus manpower; the people regarded this as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Bin proposed ending the Cao and Pu colonist levies and filling the garrisons from nearby districts with surplus troops; the people welcomed the change.

sentences.zh: 又議戶部給濱、棣、清、滄鹽券，付行省，募民以米貿之，仍增價和糴。

translations.literal: He also proposed that the Ministry of Revenue issue salt certificates for Bin, Di, Qing, and Cang, hand them to the Branch Secretariat, recruit civilians to trade grain for them, and still raise prices to buy grain at premium rates.
translations.idiomatic: He further proposed that the Ministry of Revenue issue salt certificates from the coastal salterns to the branch secretariat, recruit civilians to exchange grain for salt, and buy grain at premium prices to fill the granaries.

sentences.zh: 遠近輸販者輻輳，饋餉不勞而集。

translations.literal: Transporters from near and far converged in crowds, and provisions were gathered without exertion.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants and carriers converged from far and near, and supplies accumulated without strain.

sentences.zh: 有旨：河南四路，籍兵二萬，以益襄樊。

translations.literal: An imperial order directed that the four circuits of Henan register twenty thousand troops to reinforce Xiangyang and Fancheng.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial order called for twenty thousand troops to be levied from Henan's four circuits to reinforce the Xiangyang front.

sentences.zh: 斌即馳奏曰：「河南戶少，而調度繁多，實不堪命，減其半為宜。」

translations.literal: Bin at once sent a rapid memorial saying, "Henan has few households yet many levies and requisitions; the people truly cannot bear it—halving the quota would be fitting."
translations.idiomatic: Bin sent an urgent memorial at once: "Henan has too few households for so many demands—the people truly cannot bear it; half the levy would be right."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: His proposal was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 襄陽既下，轉嘉議大夫，仍僉行中書省。

translations.literal: After Xiangyang fell he was transferred to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and continued to serve concurrently on the Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Once Xiangyang fell he was promoted to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness while retaining his concurrent post on the Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十年，詔丞相伯顏總兵南征，改行省為河南宣慰司，加中奉大夫，賜金虎符，充宣慰使。

translations.literal: In the tenth year an edict ordered Chancellor Bayan to command the southern campaign in chief; the Branch Secretariat was changed to the Henan Pacification Commission, Bin was promoted to Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Tally, granted a gold tiger tally, and made Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In 1273 Bayan was ordered to command the southern campaign; the Henan Branch Secretariat became a Pacification Commission, and Bin was promoted to Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Tally, given a gold tiger tally, and appointed Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 是時，襄陽、正陽諸軍，悉道河南，供億雖繁，而事無缺失。

translations.literal: At that time all armies at Xiangyang, Zhengyang, and elsewhere passed through Henan; though supplies were heavy, nothing was wanting.
translations.idiomatic: All armies bound for Xiangyang and Zhengyang now passed through Henan; though the logistical burden was immense, nothing fell short.

sentences.zh: 伯顏既渡江，分阿里海牙定湖南，詔斌貳之，拜行中書省參知政事。

translations.literal: After Bayan crossed the Yangzi, Ariq Qaya was detached to pacify Hunan, and an edict ordered Bin to assist him; Bin was appointed Vice Director of the Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After Bayan crossed the Yangzi, Ariq Qaya was sent to secure Hunan with Bin as his second; Bin was appointed Vice Director of the Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 十月，圍潭州，斌攻西北鐵壩。

translations.literal: In the tenth month they besieged Tanzhou, and Bin attacked the iron palisade on the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the army besieged Tanzhou, and Bin assaulted the iron palisade on the northwest.

sentences.zh: 阿里海牙中流矢，不能軍，斌以軍夜集柵下，黎明畢登，不利。

translations.literal: Ariq Qaya was struck by an arrow and could not command; Bin gathered the army by night below the palisade, and at dawn all had climbed up, but the assault did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Ariq Qaya took an arrow wound and could not lead; Bin massed the troops beneath the palisade by night, and at dawn they had all scaled it, yet the attack failed.

sentences.zh: 斌曰：「彼軍小捷而驕弛，吾今焚其角樓，斷其援道，塹城為三周，如此則城可得。」

translations.literal: Bin said, "The enemy, having won a small victory, are arrogant and slack; if we now burn their corner towers, cut their lines of relief, and trench the walls in three rings, the city can be taken thus."
translations.idiomatic: Bin said, "They are flushed with a minor victory and grown careless. Burn their corner towers, sever their relief routes, and ring the walls with three lines of trenches—the city will fall."

sentences.zh: 諸將然之。

translations.literal: The generals agreed with him.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders assented.

sentences.zh: 乃誓師，銜枚潛登鐵壩，人齎芻秸，梯其樓火之，且豎木柵城上。

translations.literal: They then swore the army, advanced with gags in their mouths and stole up the iron palisade, each man carrying straw and stalks; they scaled the tower and set it afire, and also erected wooden palisades atop the wall.
translations.idiomatic: The army was sworn in, then advanced in silence up the iron palisade, each man carrying kindling; they scaled the tower and set it ablaze and threw up wooden palisades along the ramparts.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，布雲梯鼓譟而上，斌挾盾先登。

translations.literal: At daybreak they deployed scaling ladders and stormed upward with drums and shouts; Bin, shield in arm, was first to mount.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn scaling ladders went up amid drumbeats and war cries; Bin, shield braced before him, was the first over the wall.

sentences.zh: 阿里海牙持酒勞曰：「取此城，公之力也。」

translations.literal: Ariq Qaya brought wine to reward him and said, "The taking of this city is your achievement."
translations.idiomatic: Ariq Qaya raised a cup in tribute and said, "This city is yours—the credit is yours alone."

sentences.zh: 斌自語阿里海牙曰：「潭人膽破矣。

translations.literal: Bin said privately to Ariq Qaya, "The people of Tan have lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Bin told Ariq Qaya privately, "The defenders of Tanzhou have lost their nerve.

sentences.zh: 若斂兵不進，許其來降，則土地人民皆我有，自重湖以南，連城數十，可傳檄而定。

translations.literal: If we hold back the army and do not press forward, but allow them to come and surrender, then land and people will all be ours; from the great lakes southward, dozens of linked cities can be settled by proclamation alone.
translations.idiomatic: If we hold our troops in check and offer terms, land and people alike will be ours; south of the great lakes, dozens of walled towns will submit at the stroke of a dispatch.

sentences.zh: 若縱兵急攻，彼無噍類，得一空城何益！」

translations.literal: If we unleash the army in a furious assault, not one of them will be left alive—what good is gaining an empty city!"
translations.idiomatic: If we press a slaughtering assault, not one soul will be left—what profit is there in taking an empty shell of a city?"

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: His proposal was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 明日，即遣開示禍福，城中爭出降。

translations.literal: The next day he immediately sent men to explain fortune and disaster, and within the city they vied to come out and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he sent envoys to explain the consequences of resistance and surrender, and the city rushed to submit.

sentences.zh: 諸將怒其抗敵持久，咸欲屠之。

translations.literal: The generals were angry that the enemy had resisted so long and all wished to massacre them.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders, furious at the prolonged resistance, all wanted to slaughter the population.

sentences.zh: 斌喻以興師本意，諸將曰：「編民當如公說，敵兵必誅之。」

translations.literal: Bin explained the original purpose of raising the army; the generals said, "Registered civilians should be treated as you say, but enemy soldiers must be executed."
translations.idiomatic: Bin reminded them of the campaign's purpose; the generals replied, "Civilians should be spared as you advise, but enemy troops must die."

sentences.zh: 斌曰：「彼各為其主耳，宜旌之，以勸未附者，且殺降不祥。」

translations.literal: Bin said, "Each served his own lord—that should be honored to encourage those not yet submitted, and besides, killing those who surrender is inauspicious."
translations.idiomatic: Bin said, "Each man served his own lord—that merits honor, to encourage those still holding out, and slaughtering men who surrender brings ill fortune."

sentences.zh: 諸將乃止。

translations.literal: The generals then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders relented.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，帝嘉之，進資善大夫、行中書省左丞，潭人德之，為立生祠。

translations.literal: When news of the victory arrived the emperor praised him, promoted him to Grand Master for the Good of the State and Left Vice Director of the Branch Secretariat, and the people of Tan were grateful to him and erected a living shrine.
translations.idiomatic: Word of the victory reached the court; the emperor commended him, promoted him to Grand Master for the Good of the State and Left Vice Director of the Branch Secretariat, and the people of Tan, grateful for his mercy, built him a living shrine.

sentences.zh: 十一年，奉旨撫諭廣西，尋命還治湖南。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he received orders to pacify and instruct Guangxi, and soon afterward was commanded to return and administer Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In 1274 he was ordered to pacify Guangxi, then recalled to govern Hunan.

sentences.zh: 潭屬邑安化、湘鄉、衡山以南，賊周龍、張唐、張虎等，所在蜂起，斌駐兵南嶽。

translations.literal: In the subordinate districts of Tan—Anhua, Xiangxiang, and south of Hengshan—bandits such as Zhou Long, Zhang Tang, and Zhang Hu rose everywhere like bees; Bin stationed troops at Mount Heng.
translations.idiomatic: South of Tanzhou, in Anhua, Xiangxiang, and the country beyond Hengshan, bandits led by Zhou Long, Zhang Tang, and Zhang Hu rose everywhere; Bin encamped his forces on Mount Heng.

sentences.zh: 凡來降者，同僚議欲盡戮，以懲反側，斌但按誅其首惡，脅從者盡釋之。

translations.literal: Whenever men came to surrender, colleagues debated executing them all to warn the rebellious; Bin only punished the chief culprits according to law and released all who had been coerced.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels surrendered, his colleagues urged mass executions to deter further revolt; Bin executed only the ringleaders by law and freed all who had followed under compulsion.

sentences.zh: 十五年，被召入覲。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was summoned to court for audience.
translations.idiomatic: In 1278 he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 時阿合馬擅權日甚，廷臣莫敢誰何。

translations.literal: At that time Ahmad's monopoly of power grew daily, and court ministers dared not challenge him.
translations.idiomatic: Ahmad's grip on power was tightening daily, and no one at court dared confront him.

sentences.zh: 斌從帝至察罕腦兒。

translations.literal: Bin accompanied the emperor to Chaghan Nur.
translations.idiomatic: Bin accompanied the emperor to the summer camp at Chaghan Nur.

sentences.zh: 帝問江南各省撫治如何。

translations.literal: The emperor asked how the pacification and governance of the various provinces south of the Yangzi were proceeding.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked how the southern provinces were being governed.

sentences.zh: 斌對以治安之道在得人，今所用多非其人，因極言阿合馬姦蠹。

translations.literal: Bin answered that the way to secure order lay in getting the right men, but those now employed were mostly not such men, and he thereupon spoke at length of Ahmad's treachery and corruption.
translations.idiomatic: Bin replied that good government depended on appointing the right men, that most current appointees were unfit, and he then laid bare Ahmad's corruption in full.

sentences.zh: 帝乃令御史大夫相威、樞密副使孛羅按問之，汰其冗員，黜其親黨，檢核其不法，罷天下轉運司，海內無不稱快。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered Censor-in-Chief Xiang Wei and Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Boluo to investigate him, weed out his superfluous staff, dismiss his kin and partisans, audit his illegal acts, and abolish transport commissioners throughout the realm; within the four seas none failed to rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Censor-in-Chief Xiang Wei and Vice Director Boluo to investigate, purge Ahmad's redundant staff, dismiss his kin and cronies, audit his crimes, and abolish transport commissioners empire-wide; the realm rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 適尚書留夢炎、謝昌元言：「江淮行省事至重，而省臣無一人通文墨者。」

translations.literal: Just then the Secretariat ministers Liu Mengyan and Xie Changyuan said, "The Jianghuai Branch Secretariat affairs are weightiest of all, yet not one of its ministers is versed in letters."
translations.idiomatic: Just then Ministers Liu Mengyan and Xie Changyuan observed, "The Jianghuai Branch Secretariat is the weightiest post in the realm, yet not one of its ministers can read or write."

sentences.zh: 乃命斌遷江淮行省左丞。

translations.literal: Bin was thereupon ordered transferred to Left Vice Director of the Jianghuai Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was accordingly appointed Left Vice Director of the Jianghuai Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 既至，凡前日蠹國漁民不法之政，悉厘政之，仍條具以聞。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, all the previous policies that harmed the state and preyed on the people and were contrary to law he reformed entirely, and still set them out in articles for report to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he swept away every policy that had plundered the state and preyed on the people, itemized the reforms, and memorialized the throne.

sentences.zh: 阿合馬慮其害己，捃摭其細事，遮留使不獲上見，因誣構以罪，竟為所害。

translations.literal: Ahmad, fearing that Bin would harm him, gathered up petty matters against him, detained and blocked his envoys so he could not gain audience, and on that basis fabricated charges; in the end Bin was destroyed by him.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Bin would bring him down, Ahmad scraped together petty charges, blocked his memorials from reaching the throne, framed him on false accusations, and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 裕宗在東宮，聞之，方食，投箸惻然，遣使止之，已不及矣。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Zhenjin, in the Eastern Palace, heard of it while at his meal, cast down his chopsticks in sorrow, and sent a messenger to stop it, but it was already too late.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Zhenjin, at table in the Eastern Palace when he heard the news, dropped his chopsticks in grief and sent a messenger to halt the execution—but it was already too late.

sentences.zh: 天下冤之。

translations.literal: All under Heaven regarded it as a grievous wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The empire mourned him as a man wrongfully slain.

sentences.zh: 年五十六。

translations.literal: He was fifty-six years of age.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 至大初，贈推忠保節功臣、太傅、開府儀同三司，追封鄭國公，諡忠毅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhida era he was posthumously granted the title of Meritous Subject Who Promotes Loyalty and Preserves Integrity, Grand Preceptor, and Commissioner with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies, enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Zheng, with the posthumous name Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Zhida reign he was posthumously honored as Meritous Subject Who Promotes Loyalty and Preserves Integrity, Grand Preceptor, and Commissioner with credentials equal to the Three Excellencies, enfeoffed as Duke of Zheng, with the posthumous epithet Loyal and Resolute.

sentences.zh: 子三人，良知、威、恩。

translations.literal: He had three sons: Liangzhi, Wei, and En.
translations.idiomatic: He left three sons: Liangzhi, Wei, and En.

sentences.zh: 孫一人，敬。

translations.literal: He had one grandson, Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He had one grandson, Jing.

sentences.zh: 皆為大官。

translations.literal: All became high officials.
translations.idiomatic: All rose to high office.

sentences.zh: ○崔彧

translations.literal: ○ Cui Yu
translations.idiomatic: ○ Cui Yu

sentences.zh: 崔彧，字文卿，小字拜帖木兒，弘州人。

translations.literal: Cui Yu, style name Wenqing, childhood name Baitiemuer, was a man of Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yu, courtesy name Wenqing, also known by his childhood name Baitiemuer, came from Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 負才氣，剛直敢言，世祖甚器重之。

translations.literal: He possessed force of talent and spirit, was upright and bold in speech, and the Founder valued him highly.
translations.idiomatic: Gifted and forceful in character, upright and outspoken, he won the emperor's deep regard.

sentences.zh: 至元十六年，奉詔偕牙納木至江南，訪求藝術之人。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of the Zhiyuan era he received orders to go with Yaqumu to the south of the Yangzi to seek out men skilled in the arts.
translations.idiomatic: In 1279 he was ordered to accompany Yaqumu to the south to recruit men skilled in the arts and sciences.

sentences.zh: 明年，自江南迴，首言忽都帶兒根索亡宋財貨，煩擾百姓，身為使臣，乃挈妻子以往，所在取索鞍馬芻粟。

translations.literal: The next year, on returning from the south, he spoke first of Hududai'er Gensuo seizing the former Song's goods and wealth and troubling the people; though himself an envoy, he had taken wife and children along, and wherever he went demanded saddles, horses, fodder, and grain.
translations.idiomatic: On his return the following year he reported first that Hududai'er Gensuo was seizing former Song property and harassing the populace—though an envoy, he had brought wife and children along and extorted saddles, horses, fodder, and grain wherever he passed.

sentences.zh: 世祖雖聽其言，然虛實竟不辨決也。

translations.literal: The Founder listened to his words, yet in the end never distinguished truth from falsehood and rendered a decision.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard him out but never investigated the charges or reached a verdict.

sentences.zh: 十九年，除集賢侍讀學士。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was appointed Attendant Reader of the Hall of Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: In 1282 he was appointed Attendant Reader in the Hall of Worthies.

sentences.zh: 彧言於世祖，謂：「阿合馬當國時，同列皆知其惡，無一人孰何之者；

translations.literal: Yu said to the Founder, "When Ahmad held the state, all his colleagues knew his wickedness, yet not one confronted him;
translations.idiomatic: Yu told the emperor, "While Ahmad held power, every colleague knew his crimes, yet not one dared challenge him;

sentences.zh: 及既誅，乃各自以為潔，誠欺罔之大者。

translations.literal: after he was executed they each regarded themselves as pure—truly a great act of deception.
translations.idiomatic: yet once he was executed they each claimed to have been blameless all along—a gross deception indeed.

sentences.zh: 先有旨，凡阿合馬所用之人皆革去，臣以為守門卒隸亦不可留。

translations.literal: There was already an order that all whom Ahmad had employed were to be removed; I hold that even gate guards and runners should not be kept.
translations.idiomatic: An order already went out to dismiss everyone Ahmad had appointed; I believe even his gate guards and runners should not remain.

sentences.zh: 如參知政事阿里，請以阿散襲父職，倘使得請，其害又有不可勝言者。

translations.literal: For example, Vice Director Ali has asked that Ashan inherit his father's post; if that request were granted, the harm would again be beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Ali, for instance, has asked that his son Ashan inherit his father's post; if that were granted, the harm would be incalculable.

sentences.zh: 賴陛下神聖，灼知其奸，拒而不可。

translations.literal: Thanks to Your Majesty's divine sagacity, perceiving his treachery clearly, you refused and would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to Your Majesty's discernment, you saw through his scheme and refused.

sentences.zh: 臣已疏其奸惡十餘事，乞召阿里廷辯。」

translations.literal: I have already memorialized more than ten of his treacherous and wicked acts; I beg that Ali be summoned for court debate."
translations.idiomatic: I have already listed more than ten of his crimes; I ask that Ali be summoned to answer them at court."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「已敕中書，凡阿合馬所用，皆罷之，窮治黨與，纖悉無遺。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I have already ordered the Central Secretariat that all whom Ahmad employed are to be dismissed, his faction pursued to the end, nothing slight left out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have already ordered the Secretariat to dismiss everyone Ahmad appointed, root out his entire faction, and spare nothing.

sentences.zh: 事竟之時，朕與汝別有言也。」

translations.literal: When the matter is finished, I shall have other words for you."
translations.idiomatic: When it is done, I shall have more to say to you."

sentences.zh: 又請以郝禎剖棺戮屍，從之。

translations.literal: He also asked that Hao Zhen's coffin be opened and his corpse dismembered; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned to have Hao Zhen's coffin opened and his corpse dismembered; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 尋奉旨鉤考樞密文牘，遂由刑部尚書拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he received orders to audit the documents of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and thereupon, from Minister of Justice, was appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was ordered to audit the Bureau of Military Affairs archives, and was promoted from Minister of Justice to Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 彧言：「台臣於國家政事得失，生民休戚，百官邪正，雖王公將相，亦宜糾察。

translations.literal: Yu said, "Censors in matters of the state's gains and losses in government, the people's weal and woe, and officials' rectitude or depravity—even princes, dukes, generals, and chancellors—should also be subject to investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Yu said, "Censors exist to scrutinize the state's successes and failures in policy, the people's welfare, and officials' integrity—even princes, dukes, generals, and chancellors must answer to our scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 近唯御史得有所言，臣以為台官皆當建言，庶於國家有補。

translations.literal: Recently only investigating censors have been able to speak; I hold that all censorial officials ought to offer counsel, so that the state may benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Lately only investigating censors have been free to speak; I believe every censorial officer should offer counsel, to the state's benefit.

sentences.zh: 選用台察官，若由中書，必有偏徇之弊，御史宜從本台選擇，初用漢人十六員，今用蒙古十六員，相參巡歷為宜。」

translations.literal: In selecting surveillance officials, if done by the Central Secretariat there will surely be the abuse of partiality; investigating censors ought to be chosen from their own bureau—at first sixteen Han men were used, now sixteen Mongols are used; it would be fitting for them to tour in rotation together."
translations.idiomatic: If the Secretariat chooses surveillance officers, favoritism is inevitable; censors should be picked within the Censorate itself—sixteen Han officers at first, sixteen Mongols now—and they should tour the circuits in mixed pairs."

sentences.zh: 皆從其言。

translations.literal: All his proposals were accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor adopted all of his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 二十年，復以刑部尚書上疏，言時政十八事：一曰開廣言路，多選正人，番直上前，以司喉舌，庶免黨附壅塞之患。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, again as Minister of Justice he submitted a memorial setting forth eighteen matters of current policy: First, open wide the path of speech, select many upright men, rotate duty before the throne to serve as the ruler's voice, and thereby avoid the harm of factional attachment and obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: In 1283, again serving as Minister of Justice, he memorialized on eighteen points of policy: First, widen the channels of candid counsel, appoint upright men in rotation before the throne to speak for the court, and thus avoid the clog of faction and patronage.

sentences.zh: 二曰當阿合馬擅權，台臣莫敢糾其非，迨其事敗，然後接踵隨聲，徒取譏笑。

translations.literal: Second, when Ahmad monopolized power, censorial officials dared not correct his wrongs; only after his affair collapsed did they follow one after another in his wake, winning nothing but ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: Second, while Ahmad held unchecked power the censors dared not call out his crimes; only after his fall did they queue up to denounce him—a spectacle of ridicule.

sentences.zh: 宜別加選用，其舊人除蒙古人取聖斷外，餘皆當問罪。

translations.literal: They should be newly selected and appointed; as for the old incumbents, except Mongols left to the sacred decision, the rest should all be called to account.
translations.idiomatic: Fresh appointments are needed; of the old censors, all but Mongols—whose cases await imperial judgment—should face prosecution.

sentences.zh: 三曰樞密院定奪軍官，賞罰不當，多聽阿合馬風旨。

translations.literal: Third, the Bureau of Military Affairs decides military officers' cases, yet rewards and punishments are improper, and it often heeds Ahmad's hints.
translations.idiomatic: Third, the Bureau of Military Affairs decides officers' promotions and punishments unfairly, often at Ahmad's whispered direction.

sentences.zh: 宜擇有聲望者為長貳，庶幾號令明而賞罰當。

translations.literal: Men of reputation should be chosen as chief and deputy heads, so that orders may be clear and rewards and punishments fitting.
translations.idiomatic: Choose men of standing as the bureau's chiefs, so that orders are clear and rewards and punishments just.

sentences.zh: 四曰翰苑亦頌阿合馬功德，宜博訪南北耆儒碩望，以重此選。

translations.literal: Fourth, the Hanlin Academy also praised Ahmad's merit and virtue; widely seek out venerable scholars of great renown north and south to dignify this selection.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, the Hanlin Academy too sang Ahmad's praises; search broadly among the most eminent scholars of north and south to restore dignity to those appointments.

sentences.zh: 五曰郝禎、耿仁等雖在典刑，若是者尚多，罪同罰異，公論未伸，合次第屏除。

translations.literal: Fifth, though Hao Zhen, Geng Ren, and others have suffered the statutory penalty, many such men remain; crimes are alike but punishments differ, public opinion is not satisfied, and they should be removed in due order.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, though Hao Zhen and Geng Ren have been punished, many like them remain; equal crimes receive unequal penalties and public justice is denied—they should be removed one by one.

sentences.zh: 六曰貴遊子弟，用即顯官，幼不講學，何以從政。

translations.literal: Sixth, sons of noble houses are appointed straight to eminent offices without having studied in youth—how can they take part in government?
translations.idiomatic: Sixth, scions of great families are installed at once in high office without ever having studied—how can they govern?

sentences.zh: 得如左丞許衡教國子學，則人才輩出矣。

translations.literal: If there were men like Left Vice Director Xu Heng teaching at the Imperial Academy, talent would emerge in succession.
translations.idiomatic: With teachers like Left Vice Director Xu Heng at the Imperial Academy, men of talent would emerge in abundance.

sentences.zh: 七曰今起居注所書，不過奏事檢目而已。

translations.literal: Seventh, what the Diarists of Attendance now record is nothing more than checklists of memorials submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh, the Diarists of Attendance today record nothing but lists of memorials filed.

sentences.zh: 宜擇蒙古人之有聲望、漢人之重厚者，居其任，分番上直，帝王言動必書，以垂法於無窮。

translations.literal: Mongols of reputation and weighty, solid Han men should be chosen for the posts, rotating duty on watch; the ruler's words and acts must be written, to hand down standards without end.
translations.idiomatic: Appoint reputable Mongols and sober, weighty Han scholars, rotate them on palace duty, and record every word and act of the emperor as a model for posterity.

sentences.zh: 八曰憲曹無法可守，是以奸人無所顧忌。

translations.literal: Eighth, the legal offices have no law to uphold, and therefore wicked men have nothing to fear.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth, with no codified law for the legal offices to enforce, wrongdoers have nothing to fear.

sentences.zh: 宜定律令，以為一代之法。

translations.literal: Statutes and ordinances should be fixed to serve as the law of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Fix statutes and ordinances to serve as this dynasty's enduring law.

sentences.zh: 九曰官冗，若徒省一官員，並一衙門，亦非經久之策。

translations.literal: Ninth, offices are redundant; merely cutting one official or merging one yamen is not a lasting policy.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth, the bureaucracy is bloated; eliminating one post or merging one office is no lasting remedy.

sentences.zh: 宜參眾議，而立定成規。

translations.literal: Many opinions should be consulted and a fixed standard established.
translations.idiomatic: Consult broadly and set a permanent organizational framework.

sentences.zh: 十曰官僚無以養廉，責其貪則苛。

translations.literal: Tenth, officials have no means to sustain integrity; to blame them for greed is harsh.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth, officials lack salaries adequate to live honestly; punishing their corruption without raising their pay is unjust.

sentences.zh: 乞將諸路大小官，有俸者量增，無俸者特給。

translations.literal: I beg that officials great and small in all circuits who receive salaries have them moderately increased, and those without salaries be specially granted them.
translations.idiomatic: Raise salaries where they exist and grant stipends where none exist, for officials at every level in every circuit.

sentences.zh: 然不取之於官，惟賦之於民，蓋官吏既有所養，不致病民，少增歲賦，亦將樂從。

translations.literal: Yet it should not be taken from the offices but levied on the people—for once officials are provided for, they will not harm the people, and the people will gladly accept a small increase in annual tax.
translations.idiomatic: Fund this not from the treasury but through a modest levy on the people—once officials are properly paid they will not prey on the populace, and the people will accept a small increase in annual tax willingly.

sentences.zh: 十一曰內地百姓流移江南避賦役者，已十五萬戶。

translations.literal: Eleventh, inland commoners who have drifted to the south of the Yangzi to escape taxes and corvée already number one hundred fifty thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh, a hundred and fifty thousand inland households have fled south to escape taxes and corvée.

sentences.zh: 去家就旅，豈人之情，賦重政繁，驅之致此。

translations.literal: To leave home and become wanderers—is that human nature? Heavy taxes and tangled government have driven them to this.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving home to wander is not human nature—heavy taxes and oppressive government have driven them to it.

sentences.zh: 乞特降詔旨，招集復業，免其後來五年科役，其餘積欠並蠲，事產即日給還。

translations.literal: I beg a special edict to summon them back to their occupations, exempt their taxes and corvée for the next five years, remit all accumulated arrears, and return their property and livelihoods at once.
translations.idiomatic: Issue a special edict recalling them to their homes, exempt their taxes and corvée for five years, cancel all arrears, and restore their property immediately.

sentences.zh: 民官滿替，以戶口增耗為黜陟，其徙江南不歸者，與土著一例當役。

translations.literal: When civil officials complete their terms, promotion and demotion should depend on whether household registers increase or decline; those who moved south and do not return should bear corvée on the same terms as natives.
translations.idiomatic: Judge civil officials at term's end by whether population in their districts rose or fell; refugees who remain in the south should bear corvée like local residents.

sentences.zh: 十二曰凡丞相安童遷轉民臣，悉為阿合馬所擯黜，或居散地，或在遠方，並令拔擢。

translations.literal: Twelfth, all Han officials whom Chancellor Antong transferred and promoted were cast out by Ahmad, some placed in idle posts, some sent to distant regions—all should be promoted and selected anew.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth, every Han official Antong had advanced was driven out by Ahmad to idle posts or distant provinces—all should be restored to office.

sentences.zh: 十三曰簿錄奸黨財物，本國家之物，不可視為橫得，遂致濫用。

translations.literal: Thirteenth, goods of the traitorous faction that were inventoried belong to the state and must not be treated as windfalls, leading to reckless use.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteenth, property seized from Ahmad's faction belongs to the state, not to officials as spoils—it must not be squandered.

sentences.zh: 宜以之實帑藏、供歲計。

translations.literal: They should be used to fill the treasury stores and supply the annual budget.
translations.idiomatic: It should fill the treasury and fund the annual budget.

sentences.zh: 十四曰大都非如上都，止備巡幸，不應立留守司，此皆阿合馬以此位置私黨。

translations.literal: Fourteenth, Dadu is not like Shangdu, which exists only for imperial tours—it should not have a metropolitan garrison commission; Ahmad used this post to place his private faction.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteenth, Dadu is not Shangdu, a mere touring capital—it should not have a metropolitan garrison commission; Ahmad used that post to seat his private clique.

sentences.zh: 今宜易置總管府。

translations.literal: It should now be replaced with a Chief Commandery office.
translations.idiomatic: Replace it with a metropolitan chief commandery.

sentences.zh: 十五曰中書省右丞二，而左丞缺。

translations.literal: Fifteenth, the Central Secretariat has two right vice directors while the left vice director is vacant.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteenth, the Secretariat has two right vice directors but no left vice director.

sentences.zh: 宜改所增右丞置諸左。

translations.literal: The added right vice director should be shifted to the left.
translations.idiomatic: Move one of the right vice directors to the vacant left post.

sentences.zh: 十六曰在外行省，不必置丞相、平章，止設左右丞以下，庶幾內重，不致勢均。

translations.literal: Sixteenth, branch secretariats in the provinces need not have chancellors or grand councillors; only left and right vice directors and below should be appointed, so that the center remains weighty and power is not evenly matched.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteenth, provincial branch secretariats need no chancellors or grand councillors—only vice directors and subordinates—so the center keeps its weight and the provinces cannot rival it.

sentences.zh: 彼謂非隆其名不足鎮壓者，奸臣欺罔之論也。

translations.literal: The claim that unless titles are exalted they cannot suppress the regions is the deceitful talk of treacherous ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The argument that only exalted titles can keep the provinces in check is treacherous ministers' deceit.

sentences.zh: 十七曰阿剌海牙掌兵民之權，子侄姻黨，分列權要，官吏出其門者，十之七八，其威權不在阿合馬下。

translations.literal: Seventeenth, Alahaiya holds power over troops and people; sons, nephews, and affinal kin fill key posts, and seven or eight out of ten officials come from his gate—his authority and power are not beneath Ahmad's.
translations.idiomatic: Seventeenth, Alahaiya commands both military and civil power; his sons, nephews, and in-laws hold key posts, and seven or eight of every ten local officials are his clients—his power rivals Ahmad's.

sentences.zh: 宜罷職理算，其黨雖無污染者，亦當遷轉他所，勿使久據湖廣。

translations.literal: He should be removed from office and his accounts audited; even his faction without proven guilt should be transferred elsewhere and not allowed to hold Huguang long.
translations.idiomatic: Remove him from office and audit his accounts; even unproven associates should be transferred out of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 十八曰銓選類奏，賢否莫知。

translations.literal: Eighteenth, selections are submitted in batches and no one knows who is worthy or not.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteenth, appointments are submitted in bulk lists with no way to judge merit.

sentences.zh: 自今三品已上，必引見而後授官。

translations.literal: From now on, for rank three and above, audience must be granted before office is conferred.
translations.idiomatic: From now on every appointment of rank three or above must follow an imperial audience.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，即日命中書行其數事，餘命與御史大夫玉昔帖木兒議行之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, that same day the emperor ordered the Central Secretariat to carry out several items; the rest he commanded to be discussed and implemented with Censor-in-Chief Yeshi Temur.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was received; that day the emperor ordered the Secretariat to implement several items at once, and referred the rest to Censor-in-Chief Yeshi Temur for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 又言：「江南盜賊，相挻而起，凡二百餘所，皆由拘刷水手與造海船，民不聊生，激而成變。

translations.literal: He also said, "Bandits south of the Yangzi have risen one after another, more than two hundred groups in all, all because of the round-up of sailors and the building of sea ships—the people cannot make a living and were provoked into revolt.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported, "More than two hundred bandit bands have risen across the south, all because of the press-ganging of sailors and construction of warships—the people, driven to desperation, have rebelled.

sentences.zh: 日本之役，宜姑止之。

translations.literal: The campaign against Japan should for the present be halted.
translations.idiomatic: The invasion of Japan should be suspended for now.

sentences.zh: 又江西四省軍需，宜量民力，勿強以土產所無。

translations.literal: Moreover, military supplies for the four provinces of Jiangxi should be measured to the people's strength and not forced to include products the land does not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Military levies on Jiangxi's four provinces should match local capacity—do not demand goods the region cannot produce.

sentences.zh: 凡給物價與民者，必以實，召募水手，當從其所欲，伺民氣稍蘇，我力粗備，三二年後，東征未晚也。」

translations.literal: Whenever prices are paid to the people they must be real; in recruiting sailors their wishes should be followed; wait until popular morale has slightly revived and our strength is roughly prepared—in two or three years an eastern campaign will not be too late."
translations.idiomatic: Pay fair prices for requisitions, recruit sailors voluntarily, wait until the people recover and our forces are ready—in two or three years an eastern campaign will still be timely."

sentences.zh: 世祖以為不切，曰：「爾之所言如射然，挽弓雖可觀，發矢則非是矣。」

translations.literal: The Founder thought this impractical and said, "What you say is like archery: drawing the bow may look fine, but when the arrow is loosed it misses the mark."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dismissed this as impractical: "Your advice is like archery—the draw looks fine, but the shot goes wide."

sentences.zh: 彧又言：「昨中書奉旨，差官度量大都州縣地畝，本以革權勢兼併之弊，欲其明白，不得不於軍民諸色人戶，通行核實。

translations.literal: Yu also said, "Yesterday the Central Secretariat, by imperial order, dispatched officials to measure the fields of Dadu's prefectures and counties; the aim was to reform the abuse of powerful families' land annexation, and to make matters clear it was unavoidable to verify all military, civilian, and miscellaneous households throughout.
translations.idiomatic: Yu added, "The Secretariat recently sent officials to survey Dadu's fields to curb powerful families' land-grabs; clarity requires verifying every military, civilian, and special household.

sentences.zh: 又因取勘畜牧數目，初意本非擾民，而近者浮言胥動，恐失農時。

translations.literal: Because livestock numbers were also checked, the original intent was not to trouble the people, but recently floating rumors have stirred everywhere and I fear the farming season will be missed.
translations.idiomatic: Livestock counts were also surveyed—the intent was not to harass the people, but rumors are spreading and the planting season may be lost.

sentences.zh: 乞降旨省諭詔中書即行​​之。」

translations.literal: I beg that an edict be issued to reassure the provinces and that the Central Secretariat carry it out at once."
translations.idiomatic: Issue an edict of reassurance to the provinces and have the Secretariat execute it immediately."

sentences.zh: 又言：「建言者多，孰是孰否，中書宜集議，可行者行之，不可則明諭言者為便。」

translations.literal: He also said, "Many offer counsel—which is right and which wrong? The Central Secretariat should convene for deliberation: what can be done, do; what cannot, clearly inform the speaker—that would be convenient."
translations.idiomatic: He also urged, "Counsel pours in—the Secretariat should deliberate collectively, implement what is sound, and plainly tell petitioners when their proposals are rejected."

sentences.zh: 又言： 「各路每歲選取室女，宜罷。」

translations.literal: He also said, "The annual selection of maidens in each circuit should be abolished."
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed ending the annual selection of maidens from the circuits.

sentences.zh: 又言：「宋文思院小口斛，出入官糧，無所容隱，所宜頒行。」

translations.literal: He also said, "The small mouth-measure of the Song Wensiyuan—grain entering and leaving official stores cannot be concealed under it; it should be promulgated."
translations.idiomatic: He also urged adopting the Song Wensiyuan's standard grain measure, which prevents concealment in official granaries.

sentences.zh: 皆從之。

translations.literal: All were accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all of these as well.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，彧劾奏盧世榮不可居相職，忤旨，罷。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year Yu memorialized impeaching Lu Shirong as unfit for the chancellorship; he offended the imperial will and was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In 1284 Yu impeached Lu Shirong as unfit for chancellor; the emperor took offense and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，加集賢大學士、中奉大夫、同僉樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was given the additional titles of Grand Academician of the Hall of Worthies, Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Tally, and Associate Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1286 he was made Grand Academician of the Hall of Worthies, Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Tally, and Associate Administrator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 尋出為甘肅行省右丞。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he went out as Right Vice Director of the Gansu Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent out as Right Vice Director of the Gansu Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 召拜中書右丞。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Right Vice Director of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed Right Vice Director of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 與中書平章政事麥術丁奏曰：「近者桑哥當國四年，中外諸官，鮮有不以賄而得者。

translations.literal: Together with Grand Councillor of the Central Secretariat Maisuding he memorialized, "Recently, during the four years Sangge held the state, few officials at court or in the provinces obtained their posts without bribery.
translations.idiomatic: With Grand Councillor Maisuding he memorialized, "In Sangge's four years in power, scarcely an official at court or in the provinces won appointment without a bribe.

sentences.zh: 其昆弟故舊妻族，皆授要官美地，唯以欺蔽九重、朘削百姓為事。

translations.literal: His brothers, old friends, and wife's kin were all given key offices and fine territories, devoting themselves solely to deceiving the Ninefold Enclosure and draining the common people.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers, old friends, and in-laws received key posts and rich territories, devoting themselves solely to deceiving the throne and plundering the people.

sentences.zh: 宜令兩省嚴加考核，凡入其黨者，皆汰逐之。

translations.literal: Both secretariats should be ordered to examine strictly; all who entered his faction should be weeded out and expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Both secretariats should conduct rigorous reviews and purge everyone in his faction.

sentences.zh: 其出使之臣及按察司官受賕者，論如律，仍追宣敕，除名為民。」

translations.literal: Envoys and surveillance commissioners who accepted bribes should be punished according to law, their appointment edicts still pursued and revoked, and their names struck to commoner status."
translations.idiomatic: Envoys and surveillance commissioners who took bribes should be prosecuted, their appointment patents revoked, and their names struck from the rolls."

sentences.zh: 又奏：「桑哥所設衙門，其閒冗不急之官，徒費祿食，宜令百司集議汰罷，及自今調官，宜如舊制，避其籍貫，庶不害公。

translations.literal: They also memorialized, "The yamens Sangge established contain idle and non-urgent offices that waste only salaries; all bureaus should be ordered to deliberate and eliminate them. From now on transfers of officials should follow the old system and avoid their native districts, so that the public interest is not harmed.
translations.idiomatic: They further proposed abolishing the redundant offices Sangge had created, restoring the old rule that officials not serve in their home districts, and convening all bureaus to decide which posts to cut.

sentences.zh: 又大都高貲戶，多為桑哥所容庇，凡百徭役，止令貧民當之。

translations.literal: Moreover, wealthy households in Dadu were mostly sheltered by Sangge, and all corvée duties were laid only on the poor.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, wealthy Dadu households sheltered by Sangge escaped corvée while only the poor bore it.

sentences.zh: 今後徭役，不問何人，宜皆均輸，有敢如前以賄求人容庇者，罪之。

translations.literal: Henceforth corvée, regardless of person, should be equally distributed; whoever dares as before to seek shelter by bribery should be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth corvée should be shared equally by all; anyone who buys exemption through bribery as before should be prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 又，軍、站諸戶，每歲官吏非名取索，賦稅倍蓰，民多流移。

translations.literal: Moreover, among military and courier households, each year officials made unauthorized exactions and taxes were doubled and redoubled, and many people drifted away.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, military and courier households faced unauthorized exactions each year and taxes multiplied until many fled their homes.

sentences.zh: 請自今非奉旨及省部文學，敢私斂民及役軍匠者，論如法。

translations.literal: I beg that from now on, apart from those acting by imperial order or provincial and ministry documents, whoever dares privately to levy on the people or impress military craftsmen should be punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Prosecute anyone who levies on the people or impresses military craftsmen without imperial order or proper documentation.

sentences.zh: 又，忽都忽那顏籍戶之後，各投下毋擅招集，太宗既行之，江南民為籍已定，乞依太宗所行為是。」

translations.literal: Moreover, after Huduhu Nayan's registered households, no appanage should privately recruit people; Taizong already carried this out, and south of the Yangzi the people's registers are fixed—I beg that what Taizong enacted be followed."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, after Huduhu Nayan's household registration, no appanage should recruit subjects on its own; Taizong already forbade this, and Jiangnan's registers are fixed—follow Taizong's precedent."

sentences.zh: 皆從之。

translations.literal: All were accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all of these as well.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，由中書右丞遷御史中丞，彧奏：「太醫院使劉岳臣，嘗仕宋，練達政事，比者命其參議機務，眾皆稱善。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, from Right Vice Director of the Central Secretariat he was transferred to Censor-in-Chief; Yu memorialized, "Grand Medical Superintendent Liu Yuechen once served the Song and is thoroughly versed in government affairs; recently he was ordered to deliberate on state affairs, and all praised this.
translations.idiomatic: In 1291, promoted from Right Vice Director of the Secretariat to Censor-in-Chief, Yu memorialized, "Grand Medical Superintendent Liu Yuechen, a former Song official skilled in governance, was recently assigned to deliberate on state affairs to universal approval.

sentences.zh: 乞以為翰林學士，俾議朝政。」

translations.literal: I beg that he be made a Hanlin Academician and enabled to discuss court governance."
translations.idiomatic: Appoint him a Hanlin Academician so he may counsel on court policy."

sentences.zh: 又言：「行御史臺言：'建寧路總管馬謀，因捕盜延及平民，搒掠至死者多；

translations.literal: He also said, "The Branch Censorate reports: 'Jianning Circuit Prefect Ma Mou, while pursuing bandits, extended the net to commoners and many died under beating and torture;
translations.idiomatic: He also reported, "The Branch Censorate states that Jianning Prefect Ma Mou, while hunting bandits, tortured innocent civilians to death in large numbers;

sentences.zh: 又俘掠人財，迫通處女，受民財積百五十錠。

translations.literal: he also seized people's goods as booty, forced maidens, and accepted bribes from the people totaling one hundred fifty ingots.
translations.idiomatic: he seized property, forced women, and accepted bribes totaling a hundred and fifty ingots of silver.

sentences.zh: 獄未具，會赦。

translations.literal: The case was not concluded when an amnesty occurred.
translations.idiomatic: Before trial concluded, a general amnesty intervened.

sentences.zh: 如臣等議，馬謀以非罪殺人，不在原例。

translations.literal: As we censors hold, Ma Mou killed people without criminal cause and falls outside the amnesty precedent.
translations.idiomatic: We hold that Ma Mou killed without criminal cause and therefore falls outside the amnesty.

sentences.zh: '宜令行台詰問，明白定罪。」

translations.literal: The Branch Censorate should be ordered to interrogate him and fix guilt clearly."
translations.idiomatic: Order the Branch Censorate to interrogate him and fix his sentence."

sentences.zh: 又言：「昔行御史臺監察御史周祚，劾尚書省官忙兀帶、教化的、納速剌丁滅裡姦贓；

translations.literal: He also said, "Formerly Branch Censorate Investigating Censor Zhou Zuo impeached Secretariat officials Mamudai, Jiaohuade, and Nasuding Mili for treachery and embezzlement;
translations.idiomatic: He also recalled that Investigating Censor Zhou Zuo of the Branch Censorate had impeached Secretariat officials Mamudai, Jiaohuade, and Nasuding Mili for corruption;

sentences.zh: 納速剌丁滅裡反誣祚以罪，遣人詣尚書省告桑哥。

translations.literal: Nasuding Mili in turn falsely charged Zuo with crimes and sent men to the Secretariat to report to Sangge.
translations.idiomatic: Nasuding Mili retaliated by framing Zhou Zuo and sending agents to the Secretariat to complain to Sangge.

sentences.zh: 桑哥曖昧以聞，流祚於憨答孫，妻子家財並沒入官。

translations.literal: Sangge reported ambiguously to the throne, exiled Zuo to Qaidu's territory, and his wife, children, and family property were all confiscated by the state.
translations.idiomatic: Sangge reported evasively to the throne, exiled Zhou Zuo to Qaidu's domain, and confiscated his family and property.

sentences.zh: 祚至和林遇亂，走還京師。

translations.literal: Zuo reached Qara-qorum, encountered disorder, and fled back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Zuo reached Qara-qorum, found chaos there, and fled back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 桑哥又遣詣雲南理算錢穀，以贖其罪。

translations.literal: Sangge again sent him to Yunnan to audit finances and grain accounts, to redeem his guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Sangge then sent him to Yunnan to audit finances, supposedly to redeem his offense.

sentences.zh: 今自雲南迴，臣與省臣閱其伏詞，為罪甚微，宜復其妻子。」

translations.literal: Now, on returning from Yunnan, I and the provincial ministers reviewed his confession—the crime was very slight—and his wife and children should be restored."
translations.idiomatic: He has now returned from Yunnan; the provincial ministers and I reviewed his confession and found the offense trivial—his wife and children should be restored."

sentences.zh: 皆從之。

translations.literal: All were accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all of these as well.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，彧偕御史大夫玉昔帖木兒等奏：「四方之人，來聚闕下，率言事以乾進。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year Yu, together with Censor-in-Chief Yeshi Temur and others, memorialized, "People from the four quarters gather at the imperial gate, mostly offering counsel to seek advancement.
translations.idiomatic: In 1292 Yu joined Censor-in-Chief Yeshi Temur in memorializing, "People from every quarter crowd the capital gate, mostly petitioning for office.

sentences.zh: 國家名器，資品高下，具有定格。

translations.literal: The state's titles and insignia, and the grades of salary and rank, all have fixed standards.
translations.idiomatic: Titles, ranks, and salaries all have fixed standards.

sentences.zh: 臣等以為，中書、樞密，宜早為銓定，應格者與之，不當與者，明語其故使去。

translations.literal: We hold that the Central Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs should early fix the standards: those who qualify, grant; those who do not, clearly tell them the reason and send them away.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs should set standards at once—appoint those who qualify, and plainly tell the rest why they must leave.

sentences.zh: 又言事有是非當否，宜早與詳審言之。

translations.literal: Moreover, whether a matter is right or wrong, fitting or not, should early be examined in detail and answered.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, each proposal's merits should be examined promptly and answered clearly.

sentences.zh: 當者即議施行，或所陳有須詰難條具者，即令其人講究，否則罷遣。」

translations.literal: What is fitting should be deliberated and carried out at once; if what is presented requires questioning and itemization, let that person investigate; otherwise dismiss him."
translations.idiomatic: Sound proposals should be implemented at once; those needing clarification should be referred back to the petitioner for detail; the rest should be dismissed."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended and adopted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「納速剌丁滅裡、忻都、王巨濟，黨比桑哥，恣為不法，楮幣、銓選、鹽課、酒稅，無不更張變亂之；

translations.literal: He also memorialized, "Nasuding Mili, Xindu, and Wang Juji, cliqued with Sangge and indulged in lawlessness, overturning and disordering paper currency, selections, salt levies, and wine taxes without exception;
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized that Nasuding Mili, Xindu, and Wang Juji, Sangge's allies, had overturned paper currency, appointments, salt monopoly, and wine tax without restraint;

sentences.zh: 銜命江南，理算積久逋賦，期限嚴急，胥卒追逮，半於道路，民至嫁妻賣女，殃及親鄰，維揚、錢塘受害最慘，無故而殞其生五百餘人。

translations.literal: bearing orders in Jiangnan to audit long-overdue taxes, with deadlines harsh and urgent, clerks and runners pursuing and seizing—half of them on the roads—the people even selling wives and daughters, harm reaching kin and neighbors; Weiyang and Qiantang suffered most cruelly, and more than five hundred lives were lost without cause.
translations.idiomatic: sent to Jiangnan to collect long-overdue taxes on impossible deadlines, their runners harrying the people until wives and daughters were sold, kin and neighbors ruined—Weiyang and Qiantang suffered worst, and more than five hundred innocent lives were lost.

sentences.zh: 近者阇裡按問，悉皆首實請死，士民乃知聖天子仁愛元元，而使之至此極者，實桑哥及其凶黨之為也，莫不願食其肉。

translations.literal: Recently Chali interrogated them and all confessed truthfully and begged for death; scholars and commoners then knew the sage Son of Heaven loves the masses, and that those who brought them to this extremity were truly Sangge and his vicious faction—all wished to eat their flesh.
translations.idiomatic: Recent interrogation by Chali brought full confessions and pleas for death; the people then understood that only Sangge and his faction had driven them to such misery, and all wished to tear them apart.

sentences.zh: 臣等其議：此三人者既已伏辜，宜令中書省、御史臺從公論罪，以謝天下。」

translations.literal: Our deliberation: since these three have already paid guilt, the Central Secretariat and Censorate should punish them according to public opinion to appease all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: We propose that since these three have confessed, the Secretariat and Censorate should sentence them according to public justice to satisfy the realm."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: His proposal was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 又言：「河西人薛阇幹，領兵為宣慰，其吏詣廉訪司，告其三十六事，檄僉事簿問。

translations.literal: He also said, "Xue Shegan of Hexi, leading troops as Pacification Commissioner—his clerk went to the Surveillance Commission and reported thirty-six matters against him; a dispatch ordered the Associate Commissioner to register and question him.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported that Xue Shegan of Hexi, serving as Pacification Commissioner with military command, was accused in thirty-six counts by his clerk before the Surveillance Commission, which ordered investigation.

sentences.zh: 而薛阇幹率軍人禽問者辱之，且奪告者以去。

translations.literal: But Xue Shegan led soldiers to seize the interrogator and insult him, and also seized the accuser and took him away.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Shegan then sent soldiers to seize and humiliate the investigator and abduct the accuser.

sentences.zh: 臣議：從行台選御史往按問薛阇幹，仍先奪其職。」

translations.literal: Our deliberation: let the Branch Censorate select a censor to go investigate Xue Shegan, and first strip him of office."
translations.idiomatic: We propose that the Branch Censorate send a censor to investigate Xue Shegan and suspend him from office immediately.

sentences.zh: 又言：「行台官言：去歲桑哥既敗，使臣至自上所者，或不持璽書，口傳聖旨，縱釋有罪，擅籍人家，真偽莫辨。

translations.literal: He also said, "Branch Censorate officials report: after Sangge's fall last year, envoys coming from the imperial residence sometimes carried no sealed edicts but orally transmitted sacred commands, releasing the guilty and arbitrarily registering households—authenticity could not be distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported that after Sangge's fall, envoys from court sometimes arrived without sealed edicts, claiming oral imperial commands to free criminals and seize property—none could tell genuine from false.

sentences.zh: 臣等請：自今凡使臣，必降璽書，省、台、院諸司，必給印信文書，以杜姦欺。」

translations.literal: We beg that from now on every envoy must be given a sealed edict, and every ministry, censorate, and court bureau must issue documents with official seals, to stop treachery and fraud."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth every envoy must carry a sealed edict, and every ministry, censorate, and bureau must issue stamped documents—to end such fraud."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「何人乃敢爾耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Who would dare act thus?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor exclaimed, "Who would dare do such a thing?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「咬剌也奴、伯顏察兒，比嘗傳旨縱罪人。」

translations.literal: They answered, "Yaraliyanu and Bayanchar—recently they transmitted orders to release criminals."
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "Yaraliyanu and Bayanchar have recently claimed oral orders to free criminals."

sentences.zh: 帝悉可其奏。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all their memorials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved every proposal.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「松州達魯花赤長孫，自言不願為錢穀官，願備員廉訪司，令木八剌沙上聞。

translations.literal: He also memorialized, "Changsun, darughachi of Songzhou, says himself he does not wish to be a finance official but wishes to serve as a reserve member of the Surveillance Commission—order Mubalisha to report this upward.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported that Changsun, darughachi of Songzhou, had declined a finance post and asked to serve on the Surveillance Commission—order Mubalisha to report this to the throne.

sentences.zh: 傳旨至臺，特令委用，臺臣所宜奉行。

translations.literal: When the transmitted order reached the Censorate, it specially ordered his appointment; censorate officials ought to carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Once the order reached the Censorate appointing him, the censors were expected to implement it.

sentences.zh: 但徑自陳獻，又且嘗有罪，理應區別。」

translations.literal: But he presented himself directly without going through proper channels, and moreover had once committed an offense; reason demands a distinction."
translations.idiomatic: Yet he had petitioned on his own initiative and had a prior offense on his record, so the case deserved separate handling.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此自卿事，宜審行之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "This is your own affair; you should carefully carry it out."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "That is for you to decide—handle it with care."

sentences.zh: 又奏：「江南李淦言葉李過愆，被旨赴京以辯，今葉李物故，事有不待辨者。

translations.literal: He also memorialized, "Li Gan of Jiangnan accused Ye Li of misconduct; Ye Li was ordered to come to the capital to defend himself. Now Ye Li has died, and the matter no longer needs adjudication.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported that Li Gan of Jiangnan had accused Ye Li of wrongdoing and that Ye Li had been summoned to the capital to answer the charge—but Ye Li was now dead, so the case need no longer be pursued.

sentences.zh: 李淦本儒人，請授以教官，旌其直言。」

translations.literal: Li Gan was originally a Confucian scholar; I request that he be appointed an instructor to honor his forthright speech."
translations.idiomatic: Li Gan was a scholar by background; I ask that he be given a teaching post to reward his candid remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「鄂州一道，舊有按察司，要束木惡其害己，令桑哥奏罷之。

translations.literal: He also memorialized, "The Ezhou circuit formerly had a Surveillance Commission; Yao Shumu hated that it harmed him and had Sangge memorialize to abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed restoring the Surveillance Commission in the Ezhou circuit, which Yao Shumu had persuaded Sangge to abolish because it threatened his interests.

sentences.zh: 臣觀鄂州等九郡，境土亦廣，宜復置廉訪司。

translations.literal: Your subject observes that Ezhou and eight other prefectures cover broad territory; the Surveillance Commission should be restored.
translations.idiomatic: Ezhou and the eight neighboring prefectures span a wide area and should again have a Surveillance Commission.

sentences.zh: 行御史臺舊治揚州，今揚州隸南京，而行台移治建康；

translations.literal: The Branch Censorate was formerly based at Yangzhou; now Yangzhou belongs to Nanjing, and the Branch Censorate should move to Jiankang;
translations.idiomatic: The Branch Censorate had been stationed at Yangzhou, but since Yangzhou now falls under Nanjing, the branch should relocate to Jiankang;

sentences.zh: 其淮東廉訪司舊治淮安，今宜移治揚州。」

translations.literal: The Huaidong Surveillance Commission was formerly based at Huai'an; now it should move to Yangzhou."
translations.idiomatic: and the Huaidong Surveillance Commission, formerly at Huai'an, should move to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「諸官吏受賕，在朝則詣御史臺首告，在外則詣按察司首告，已有成憲。

translations.literal: He also memorialized, "When officials accept bribes, in the capital they report first to the Censorate, and outside they report first to the Surveillance Commission—this is established law.
translations.idiomatic: He also reminded the throne that bribery cases were long governed by fixed rules: reports in the capital went to the Censorate, and in the provinces to the Surveillance Commission.

sentences.zh: 自桑哥持國，受賕者不赴憲台憲司，而詣諸司首，故爾反覆牽延，事久不竟。

translations.literal: Since Sangge held power, those who accepted bribes did not go to the censorate or surveillance offices but reported to various ministries; hence cases dragged back and forth and were long left unfinished.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sangge, bribery complaints were routed to ordinary ministries instead of the censorate, so cases bounced endlessly and rarely reached a conclusion.

sentences.zh: 臣謂宜如前旨，惟於本台、行台及諸道廉訪司首告，諸司無得輒受。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that, as in the former order, reports should be made only to the central censorate, branch censorate, and circuit Surveillance Commissions; other ministries must not accept them at will.
translations.idiomatic: I propose restoring the old rule: complaints may be filed only with the central or branch censorate or a circuit Surveillance Commission, and no other office may take them.

sentences.zh: 又監察御史塔的失言：女直人教化的，去歲東征，妄言以米千石餉阇裡鐵木兒軍萬人，奏支鈔四百錠，宜令本處廉訪司究問，與本處行省追償議罪。」

translations.literal: Supervising Censor Tadishi also reported: Jiaohua, a Jurchen, on last year's eastern campaign falsely claimed to supply ten thousand troops under Jelme with a thousand shi of grain and memorialized for four hundred ingots of paper money; the local Surveillance Commission should investigate, and the local Branch Secretariat should recover the funds and determine punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor Tadishi also accused the Jurchen Jiaohua of fabricating a claim that he had fed ten thousand of Jelme's troops with a thousand shi of grain during last year's eastern campaign, for which he had drawn four hundred ingots of paper money—the local Surveillance Commission should investigate, and the Branch Secretariat should recover the money and fix his penalty.

sentences.zh: 皆從之。

translations.literal: All were accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all of these as well.

sentences.zh: 三月，中書省臣奏，請以彧為右丞，世祖曰：「崔彧不愛於言，惟可使任言責。」

translations.literal: In the third month, Secretariat officials memorialized to appoint Yu as Right Vice Chancellor; Kublai said, "Cui Yu does not delight in rhetoric—he can only be entrusted with the duty of remonstrance."
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Secretariat proposed making Cui Yu Right Vice Chancellor, but Kublai replied, "Cui Yu is no court rhetorician; he is fit only for the censor's role of speaking truth to power."

sentences.zh: 閏六月，又同御史大夫玉昔帖木兒奏：「近耿熙告：河間鹽運司官吏盜官庫錢，省台遣人同告者雜問，凡負二萬二千餘錠，已徵八千九百餘錠，猶欠一萬三千一百餘錠。

translations.literal: In the intercalary sixth month, together with Censor-in-Chief Yeshi Temür he memorialized, "Recently Geng Xi reported that officials of the Hejian Salt Transport Office stole treasury funds; the secretariat and censorate sent men to question him together with the accuser. The total debt exceeds twenty-two thousand ingots; eight thousand nine hundred plus have been collected, and more than thirteen thousand one hundred remain owed.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary sixth month he and Censor-in-Chief Yeshi Temür reported Geng Xi's accusation that Hejian Salt Transport officials had embezzled treasury funds. After joint inquiry by the secretariat and censorate, the debt stood at over twenty-two thousand ingots, of which fewer than nine thousand had been recovered and more than thirteen thousand were still outstanding.

sentences.zh: 運使張庸，嘗獻其妹於阿合馬，有寵；

translations.literal: Transport Commissioner Zhang Yong once presented his younger sister to Ahmad and gained favor;
translations.idiomatic: Transport Commissioner Zhang Yong had once offered his sister to Ahmad and won his patronage;

sentences.zh: 阿合馬既沒，以官婢事桑哥，復有寵。

translations.literal: After Ahmad died, he gave an official maidservant to serve Sangge and again gained favor.
translations.idiomatic: and after Ahmad's death he placed an official maidservant in Sangge's household and regained favor.

sentences.zh: 故庸夤緣戚屬，得久居漕司，獨盜三千一百錠。

translations.literal: Thus Yong relied on kinship connections to remain long at the transport office and alone embezzled three thousand one hundred ingots.
translations.idiomatic: Through these connections Yong had kept his post at the transport office for years and personally embezzled three thousand one hundred ingots.

sentences.zh: 臣等議：宜命台省遣官，同廉訪司倍征之。」

translations.literal: We deliberated: the censorate and secretariat should dispatch officials with the Surveillance Commission to levy double recovery."
translations.idiomatic: We recommend that the censorate and secretariat send officials with the Surveillance Commission to recover twice the amount owed.

sentences.zh: 又言：「月林伯察江西廉訪司官術兒赤帶、河東廉訪司官忽兒赤，擅縱盜賊，抑奪民田，貪污不法，今月林伯以事至京，宜就令詰問。」

translations.literal: He also said, "Yuelin Bo inspected Surveillance officials Shier Chidai of Jiangxi and Hu'erchi of Hedong, who freely allowed bandits, seized peasant land, and were corrupt and unlawful. Now Yuelin Bo has come to the capital on business; he should be questioned on the spot."
translations.idiomatic: He also charged that Yuelin Bo had found Jiangxi Surveillance official Shier Chidai and Hedong Surveillance official Hu'erchi guilty of sheltering bandits, seizing farmland, and gross corruption—and since Yuelin Bo was now in the capital, he should be interrogated immediately.

sentences.zh: 又言：「揚州鹽運司受財，多付商賈鹽，計直該鈔二萬二千八百錠，臣等以謂追徵足日，課以歸省，贓以歸台，斟酌定罪，以清蠹源。」

translations.literal: He also said, "The Yangzhou Salt Transport Office accepted bribes and issued excessive merchant salt worth twenty-two thousand eight hundred ingots of paper money. We hold that once full recovery is made, revenue should go to the secretariat and illicit gains to the censorate, with punishment determined appropriately to clean the source of corruption."
