translations.idiomatic: He also reported that the Yangzhou Salt Transport Office had taken bribes and issued excess salt to merchants worth twenty-two thousand eight hundred ingots; once the money was recovered, the revenue should go to the secretariat and the bribes to the censorate, with penalties fixed accordingly to uproot the corruption.

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: All were approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all of these proposals as well.

sentences.zh: 又奏：「江西詹玉，始以妖術致位集賢。

translations.literal: He also memorialized, "Zhan Yu of Jiangxi first gained a post in the Academy of Scholarly Worthies through sorcery.
translations.idiomatic: He also accused Zhan Yu of Jiangxi of rising to a post in the Academy of Scholarly Worthies through occult arts.

sentences.zh: 當桑哥持國，遣其掊核江西學糧，貪酷暴橫，學校大廢。

translations.literal: When Sangge held power, he sent him to audit Jiangxi school grain funds; he was greedy, cruel, and violent, and schools were greatly ruined.
translations.idiomatic: While Sangge was in power he had sent Zhan Yu to squeeze Jiangxi school funds; his greed and brutality devastated the schools.

sentences.zh: 近與臣言：撒里蠻、答失蠻傳旨，以江南有謀叛者，俾乘傳往鞫；

translations.literal: Recently he told your subject: Sariman and Dashiman transmitted an order that there were rebels plotting in Jiangnan and sent him post-haste to investigate;
translations.idiomatic: He recently told me that Sariman and Dashiman had claimed an imperial order that rebels were plotting in Jiangnan and had dispatched him post-haste to investigate;

sentences.zh: 明日，訪知為禿速忽、香山欺罔奏遣。

translations.literal: The next day it was learned that Tusuhu and Xiangshan had deceived the throne with a false memorial sending him.
translations.idiomatic: but the next day it emerged that Tusuhu and Xiangshan had fabricated the charge and sent him off under false pretenses.

sentences.zh: 玉在京師，猶敢誑誕如此，宜亟追還訊問。」

translations.literal: Yu is in the capital yet still dares to deceive so flagrantly; he should be urgently recalled and interrogated."
translations.idiomatic: Zhan Yu is still in the capital and brazenly spinning such lies; he should be recalled at once and questioned.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此惡人也，遣之往者，朕未嘗知之。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "This is an evil man; as for sending him—I never knew of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "He is a wicked man—and I never authorized sending him.

sentences.zh: 其亟禽以來。」

translations.literal: Have him seized and brought immediately."
translations.idiomatic: Seize him and bring him here at once."

sentences.zh: 三十年，彧言：「大都民食唯仰客糴，頃緣官括商船載遞諸物，致販鬻者少，米價翔踴。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, Yu reported, "The people of Dadu rely solely on grain brought by merchants; recently because officials requisitioned merchant ships to transport various goods, sellers grew scarce and grain prices soared.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year Cui Yu warned that Dadu depended entirely on grain merchants, but recent official requisitioning of merchant ships for transport had driven sellers away and sent rice prices soaring.

sentences.zh: 臣等議：勿令有司括船為便。」

translations.literal: We deliberated: it would be best not to let government offices requisition ships."
translations.idiomatic: We recommended ending official ship requisitions.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: His proposal was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是彧居御史臺久，又守正不阿，以故人疾之，監察御史斡羅失剌，劾奏「中丞崔彧，兄在先朝嘗有罪，還其所籍家產非宜」等事，成宗怒其妄言，笞而遣之。

translations.literal: Thus Yu had long served at the Censorate and, upright and unyielding, was therefore resented. Supervising Censor Woluo Shila impeached Vice Censor-in-Chief Cui Yu on grounds including that his brother had committed an offense in the previous reign and restoring his confiscated family property was improper. Temür, angered by the baseless charge, had him flogged and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yu had served the Censorate for many years with uncompromising integrity, which made him enemies. Supervising Censor Woluo Shila then impeached him, claiming among other things that restoring his brother's confiscated property from the previous reign was improper. Temür, furious at the spurious attack, had Woluo Shila flogged and expelled.

sentences.zh: 十一月，御史臺奏：「大都路總管沙的，盜支官錢，及受贓計五千三百緡，準律當杖百七，不敘，以故臣子從輕論。」

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the Censorate memorialized, "Dadu Circuit intendant Sha Di embezzled official funds and accepted bribes totaling five thousand three hundred strings; by law he deserves one hundred seven strokes of the rod and permanent disqualification, but as a former minister's son he should receive lighter punishment."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the Censorate reported that Dadu Circuit intendant Sha Di had embezzled public funds and taken bribes worth five thousand three hundred strings—a crime normally punished with one hundred seven strokes and permanent ban from office, though as a former minister's son he merited a lighter sentence.

sentences.zh: 而成宗欲止權停其職，彧與御史大夫只而合郎執不可。

translations.literal: But Temür wished only to suspend him from office temporarily; Yu and Censor-in-Chief Zhihe Helang firmly objected.
translations.idiomatic: Temür wanted merely to suspend Sha Di from office, but Cui Yu and Censor-in-Chief Zhihe Helang refused to accept so lenient a penalty.

sentences.zh: 已而御史又奏：「彧任中丞且十年，非所宜。」

translations.literal: Soon after the censors memorialized, "Yu has served as vice censor-in-chief for nearly ten years—not appropriate."
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the censors memorialized that Cui Yu had held the vice censor-in-chief post for nearly ten years and ought to be replaced.

sentences.zh: 彧遂以病辭，成宗諭之曰：「卿之辭退，誠是已，然勉為朕少留之。」

translations.literal: Yu then resigned citing illness; Temür instructed him, "Your wish to retire is indeed justified, yet strive to remain a little longer for me."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yu then resigned on grounds of illness. Temür told him, "Your request is reasonable, but try to stay a while longer for my sake."

sentences.zh: 閏十二月，兼領侍儀司事，與太常卿劉無隱奏：「新正朝賀，歲常習儀大萬安寺。」

translations.literal: In the intercalary twelfth month, concurrently heading the Ceremonial Office, he memorialized with Director of Court Ceremonies Liu Wuyin, "For New Year's court congratulations, the yearly rehearsal is held at Dawan'an Temple."
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary twelfth month, while also directing the Ceremonial Office, he and Director of Court Ceremonies Liu Wuyin reported that the annual New Year's rehearsal was held at Dawan'an Temple.

sentences.zh: 成宗曰：「去歲兀都帶以雪故來後，今而復然。

translations.literal: Temür said, "Last year Orduqai arrived late because of snow; now it happens again.
translations.idiomatic: Temür remarked, "Last year Orduqai arrived late because of snow, and the same thing is happening again.

sentences.zh: 諸不至及失儀者，殿中司、監察御史同糾之。」

translations.literal: Those who fail to arrive or breach protocol—the Palace Administration and supervising censors shall jointly impeach them."
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who failed to attend or breached protocol would be impeached jointly by the Palace Administration and the supervising censors."

sentences.zh: 二年，加榮祿大夫、平章政事，尋與御史大夫禿赤奏：「世祖聖訓，凡在籍儒人，皆復其家。

translations.literal: In the second year he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Grand Councillor; soon he and Censor-in-Chief Tuochi memorialized, "Kublai's sacred instruction: all registered scholars should have their households restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Grand Councillor, and soon he and Censor-in-Chief Tuochi reminded the throne of Kublai's decree that all registered scholars were to have their households restored.

sentences.zh: 今歲月滋久，老者已矣，少者不學，宜遵先制，俾廉訪司常加勉勵。」

translations.literal: Now years pass, the old have died, the young do not study; the former system should be followed and Surveillance Commissions should regularly encourage them."
translations.idiomatic: Years had passed, the elders were gone, and the young no longer studied; they urged a return to the old policy with Surveillance Commissions charged to encourage learning.

sentences.zh: 成宗深然之，命彧與不忽木、阿里渾撒里同翰林、集賢議，特降詔條，使作成人材，以備選舉。

translations.literal: Temür strongly agreed and ordered Yu, with Buqa, Arghun Sali, the Hanlin Academy, and the Academy of Scholarly Worthies to deliberate and issue special edict provisions to nurture talent for selection.
translations.idiomatic: Temür wholeheartedly agreed and ordered Cui Yu, Buqa, and Arghun Sali to consult with the Hanlin Academy and the Academy of Scholarly Worthies on special edict provisions to cultivate talent for future appointment.

sentences.zh: 彧以是歲九月卒。

translations.literal: Yu died in the ninth month of that year.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yu died that September.

sentences.zh: 至大元年七月，贈推誠履正功臣、太傅、開府儀同三司，追封鄭國公，諡忠肅。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Zhida, he was posthumously granted Honored Minister Who Sincerely Upholds Integrity, Grand Tutor, and Grand Master of the Palace with Same Threefold Honors as the Three Excellencies; posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Zheng; temple name Loyal and Solemn.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the first year of Zhida he was posthumously honored as Honored Minister Who Sincerely Upholds Integrity, Grand Tutor, and Palace Minister of the First Rank, enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Zheng, and given the temple name Zhongsu.

sentences.zh: ○葉李

translations.literal: ○ Ye Li
translations.idiomatic: Biography: Ye Li

sentences.zh: 葉李，字太白，一字舜玉，杭州人。

translations.literal: Ye Li, style name Taibai, also styled Shunyu, was a man of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Li, courtesy name Taibai and also known as Shunyu, was from Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 少有奇質，從學於太學博士義烏施南學，補京學生。

translations.literal: From youth he had remarkable gifts; he studied under Imperial Academy Doctor Shi Nanxue of Yiwu and was enrolled as a capital academy student.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a youth he showed unusual promise. He studied under Shi Nanxue, a doctor of the Imperial Academy from Yiwu, and was admitted as a student at the capital academy.

sentences.zh: 宋景定五年，彗出於柳，理宗下詔罪己，求直言。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jingding of Song, a comet appeared in the Willow constellation; Emperor Lizong issued a self-reproach edict seeking frank counsel.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the Song Jingding era, a comet appeared in the Willow constellation, and Emperor Lizong issued an edict blaming himself and calling for candid criticism.

sentences.zh: 是時，世祖南伐，駐師江上，宋命賈似道領兵御之。

translations.literal: At that time Kublai was campaigning south and encamped on the Yangtze; Song ordered Jia Sidao to lead troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai was then campaigning south with his army on the Yangtze, and the Song court sent Jia Sidao to command the defense.

sentences.zh: 會憲宗崩，世祖班師，鄂州圍解。

translations.literal: When Möngke died, Kublai withdrew his army, and the siege of Ezhou was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: When Möngke died, Kublai withdrew, and the siege of Ezhou was broken off.

sentences.zh: 似道自詭以為己功，因復入相，益驕肆自顓，創置公田關子，其法病民甚，中外毋敢指議。

translations.literal: Jia Sidao falsely claimed the credit, returned to the chancellorship, grew more arrogant and autocratic, and created the public-field note system, which greatly harmed the people; none at court or in the provinces dared criticize it.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Sidao falsely claimed the victory as his own, returned to power, and grew ever more arrogant and domineering. He introduced the public-field note system, which deeply harmed the people, and no one at court or in the provinces dared speak against it.

sentences.zh: 李乃與同舍生康棣​​而下八十三人，伏闕上書，攻似道，其略曰：「三光舛錯，宰執之愆。

translations.literal: Ye Li and eighty-three fellow students including Kang Di submitted a petition at the palace gate attacking Jia Sidao, summarizing: "The three luminaries are misaligned—the fault lies with the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Li joined eighty-three fellow students, including Kang Di, in submitting a memorial at the palace gate denouncing Jia Sidao. It opened: "Heaven's signs are out of order—the fault lies with those who hold power.

sentences.zh: 似道繆司台鼎，變亂紀綱，毒害生靈，神人共怒，以乾天譴。」

translations.literal: Jia Sidao wrongly holds the tripod of state, overturns law and order, poisons the people; gods and men share the outrage, drawing heavenly punishment."
translations.idiomatic: Jia Sidao has usurped the seat of power, overturned law and order, and poisoned the people. Gods and men alike are enraged, and heaven itself has sent this warning."

sentences.zh: 似道大怒，知書稿出於李，嗾其黨臨安尹劉良貴，誣李僭用金飾齋扁，鍛煉成獄，竄漳州。

translations.literal: Jia Sidao was furious, learning the draft came from Ye Li; he incited his ally Lin'an Prefect Liu Lianggui to accuse Ye Li of usurping privilege by gilding his study plaque, forged a case, and banished him to Zhangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Sidao was enraged when he learned Ye Li had written the memorial. He set his ally Liu Lianggui, prefect of Lin'an, to accuse Ye Li of improperly gilding his study plaque, fabricated a case, and had him exiled to Zhangzhou.

sentences.zh: 似道既敗，乃得自便。

translations.literal: After Jia Sidao's fall, he was finally freed.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Jia Sidao's downfall was Ye Li finally released.

sentences.zh: 會宋亡，歸隱富春山。

translations.literal: When Song fell, he retired to seclusion on Fuchun Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song dynasty fell, he withdrew to live in seclusion on Fuchun Mountain.

sentences.zh: 江淮行省及宣、憲兩司爭辟之，署蘇、杭、常等郡教授，俱不應。

translations.literal: The Jianghuai Branch Secretariat and the Pacification and Surveillance offices competed to recruit him, appointing him professor for Suzhou, Hangzhou, Changzhou, and other prefectures—all of which he declined.
translations.idiomatic: The Jianghuai Branch Secretariat and the Pacification and Surveillance offices vied to recruit him and offered him professorships in Suzhou, Hangzhou, Changzhou, and other prefectures, but he refused them all.

sentences.zh: 至元十四年，世祖命御史大夫相威行台江南，且求遺逸，以李姓名上。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan, Kublai ordered Censor-in-Chief Xiangwei to tour Jiangnan with the Branch Censorate and seek recluses; Ye Li's name was submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan, Kublai sent Censor-in-Chief Xiangwei to tour Jiangnan with the Branch Censorate in search of hidden talent, and Ye Li's name was brought forward.

sentences.zh: 初，李攻似道書，其末有「前年之師，適有天幸，克成厥勳」之語，世祖習聞之，每拊掌稱嘆。

translations.literal: Earlier, in Ye Li's petition against Jia Sidao, the closing line read, "The campaign of two years ago succeeded by heaven's fortune and achieved its merit"; Kublai had often heard it and clapped his hands in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai had long known Ye Li's memorial against Jia Sidao, especially its closing line that the campaign two years before had succeeded only by heaven's luck—and each time he heard it he clapped his hands in admiration.

sentences.zh: 及是，其姓名聞，世祖大悅，即授奉訓大夫、浙西道儒學提舉。

translations.literal: When his name came up, Kublai was greatly pleased and immediately appointed him Gentleman for Advancing Culture and Zhexi Circuit Confucian Intendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Ye Li's name reached him, Kublai was delighted and immediately appointed him Gentleman for Advancing Culture and Confucian Intendant of the Zhexi Circuit.

sentences.zh: 李聞命，欲遁去，而使者致丞相安童書，有云：「先生在宋，以忠言讜論著稱，簡在帝心。

translations.literal: Ye Li, on receiving the appointment, wished to flee; but the envoy brought a letter from Chancellor Antong saying, "The Master in Song was renowned for loyal, forthright counsel and is selected in the emperor's heart.
translations.idiomatic: On hearing the appointment, Ye Li tried to slip away, but the envoy delivered a letter from Chancellor Antong: "In the Song you were known for loyal and forthright counsel, and you have long been in the emperor's mind.

sentences.zh: 今授以五品秩，士君子當隱見隨時，其尚悉心，以報殊遇。」

translations.literal: Now granted fifth-rank office, a gentleman of integrity should serve or withdraw as times require; devote yourself fully to repay this exceptional favor."
translations.idiomatic: You are now offered fifth-rank office. A true gentleman serves or withdraws as the times demand. Give yourself wholeheartedly to repaying this extraordinary honor."

sentences.zh: 李乃幡然北向再拜曰：「仕而得行其言，此臣夙心也，敢不奉詔！」

translations.literal: Ye Li then turned north, bowed twice, and said, "To serve and put my words into practice—this has long been my heart's desire; how dare I not obey the edict!"
translations.idiomatic: Ye Li then turned north, bowed twice, and said, "To serve and finally speak my mind—this has been my lifelong wish. How could I refuse the edict!"

sentences.zh: 二十三年，侍御史程文海，奉命搜賢江南。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, Attending Censor Cheng Wenhai was ordered to seek worthy men in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year Attending Censor Cheng Wenhai was dispatched to search Jiangnan for talent.

sentences.zh: 世祖諭之曰：「此行必致葉李來。」

translations.literal: Kublai instructed him, "This mission must bring Ye Li."
translations.idiomatic: Kublai told him, "This mission must not return without Ye Li."

sentences.zh: 李既至京師，敕集賢大學士阿魯渾撒里館於院中。

translations.literal: When Ye Li reached the capital, Kublai ordered Hanlin Academician Aruqan Sali to lodge him in the academy.
translations.idiomatic: When Ye Li arrived in the capital, Kublai ordered Academician Aruqan Sali of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies to host him at the academy.

sentences.zh: 它日，召見披香殿，勞問「卿遠來良苦」，且曰：「卿向時訟似道書，朕賞識之。」

translations.literal: Another day he was summoned to Pichiang Hall; Kublai expressed sympathy for the long journey and said, "Your petition against Jia Sidao—I appreciated it."
translations.idiomatic: On another day Kublai received him in Pichiang Hall, commiserated over the long journey, and said, "I have long admired your memorial against Jia Sidao."

sentences.zh: 更詢以治道安出。

translations.literal: He further asked where good governance should begin.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked where sound governance should begin.

sentences.zh: 李歷陳古帝王得失成敗之由，世祖首肯，賜坐錫宴，更命五日一入議事。

translations.literal: Ye Li enumerated the causes of ancient emperors' success and failure; Kublai nodded assent, granted him a seat and feast, and ordered him to attend deliberations every five days.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Li traced the rise and fall of ancient rulers in detail. Kublai nodded in agreement, seated him at a banquet, and ordered him to attend court deliberations every five days.

sentences.zh: 時各道儒司悉以曠官罷，李因奏曰：「臣欽睹先帝詔書，當創業時，軍務繁夥，尚招致士類。

translations.literal: At that time all circuit Confucian offices had been abolished for long vacancies; Ye Li memorialized, "Your subject reverently saw the late emperor's edict: even amid founding campaigns and heavy military affairs, he still summoned scholars.
translations.idiomatic: At the time all circuit Confucian offices had been abolished for standing vacant. Ye Li memorialized, "I have read the late emperor's edict: even in the founding years, when military affairs were overwhelming, he still sought out scholars.

sentences.zh: 今陛下混一區宇，偃武修文，可不作養人才，以弘治道？

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty has unified the realm and turned from war to culture—how can we not nurture talent to expand the way of governance?
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty has unified the realm and turned from war to culture. How can we fail to cultivate talent and broaden the way of governance?

sentences.zh: 各道儒學提舉及郡教授，實風化所繫，不宜罷。

translations.literal: Circuit Confucian intendants and prefectural professors are essential to moral transformation and should not be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit Confucian intendants and prefectural professors are vital to civilizing the people and should not have been abolished.

sentences.zh: 請復立提舉司，專提調學官，課諸生，講明治道，而上其成才者於太學，以備錄用。

translations.literal: I request restoring the Intendant Office to oversee school officials, examine students, teach governance, and send accomplished ones to the Imperial Academy for selection.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the Intendant Office be restored to supervise school officials, examine students, teach the principles of governance, and send the most promising to the Imperial Academy for future appointment.

sentences.zh: 凡儒戶徭役，乞一切蠲免。」

translations.literal: I request complete exemption of corvée for scholarly households."
translations.idiomatic: I also ask that corvée duties on scholarly households be abolished entirely."

sentences.zh: 可其奏。

translations.literal: His memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 是時，乃顏叛北邊，詔李庭出師討之，而將校多用國人，或其親暱，立馬相向語，輒釋仗不戰，逡巡退卻。

translations.literal: At that time Nayan rebelled in the north; Li Ting was ordered to campaign against him, but commanders were mostly Mongols or their kin—they would speak face to face on horseback and drop their weapons without fighting, then withdraw hesitantly.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Nayan rebelled in the north, and Li Ting was sent to suppress him. But the commanders were mostly Mongols or their relatives; they would ride up, talk face to face, lay down their arms without fighting, and then drift away.

sentences.zh: 帝患之。

translations.literal: The emperor was troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 李密啟曰：「兵貴奇，不貴眾，臨敵當以計取。

translations.literal: Ye Li privately reported, "Warfare values surprise, not numbers; confronting the enemy one should win by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Li privately advised, "In war, surprise matters more than numbers. One defeats the enemy by strategy.

sentences.zh: 彼既親暱，誰肯盡力？

translations.literal: Since they are kin, who will fight hard?
translations.idiomatic: When commanders are relatives, who will fight with all his strength?

sentences.zh: 徒費陛下糧餉，四方轉輸甚勞。

translations.literal: It wastes Your Majesty's provisions, and transport from all directions is greatly burdensome.
translations.idiomatic: It wastes Your Majesty's supplies and burdens transport from every quarter.

sentences.zh: 臣前用漢軍列前步戰，而聯大車斷其後，以示死鬥。

translations.literal: Your subject previously placed Han troops in front for infantry battle and linked wagons behind to cut off retreat, showing they must fight to the death.
translations.idiomatic: I would place Han infantry in the front ranks and line wagons behind them to block retreat, forcing a fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 彼嘗玩我，必不設備，我以大眾踣之，無不勝矣。」

translations.literal: They have treated us lightly and will not prepare; a mass assault will crush them without fail."
translations.idiomatic: They have grown contemptuous of us and will be unprepared. A full assault will overwhelm them."

sentences.zh: 帝以其謀諭將帥，師果奏捷。

translations.literal: The emperor relayed his plan to the generals; the army soon reported victory.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor passed Ye Li's plan to the commanders, and the army soon reported victory.

sentences.zh: 自是帝益奇李，每罷朝，必召見論事。

translations.literal: From then the emperor prized Ye Li more; after every court session he summoned him to discuss affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Kublai valued Ye Li all the more and summoned him after every court session to discuss state affairs.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，特拜御史中丞，兼商議中書省事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, he was specially appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief and concurrently deliberator of Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he was specially appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief with concurrent duty to deliberate Secretariat business.

sentences.zh: 李固辭曰：「臣本羈旅，荷蒙眷知，使備顧問，固當竭盡愚衷。

translations.literal: Ye Li firmly declined, saying, "Your subject is but a sojourner, graciously favored as adviser—I should devote my utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Li firmly declined, saying, "I am only a guest in your service, yet you have honored me as an adviser. I would give you my best counsel.

sentences.zh: 御史臺總察中外機務，臣愚不足當此任。

translations.literal: The Censorate oversees all internal and external affairs; your subject's dull wit cannot bear this duty.
translations.idiomatic: But the Censorate oversees affairs throughout the realm, and I am not equal to such a post.

sentences.zh: 且臣昔竄瘴鄉，素染足疾，比歲尤劇。」

translations.literal: Moreover I was once exiled to malarial country and have long suffered foot ailment, worse this year."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, I was once exiled to the malarial south and have long suffered from foot ailment, which has grown worse in recent years."

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「卿足艱於行，心豈不可行耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor smiled and said, "Your feet find walking hard—surely your heart can still serve?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor smiled and said, "Your feet may find walking difficult, but surely your heart is still fit for service?"

sentences.zh: 李固辭，得許。

translations.literal: Ye Li declined again and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Li declined again, and the emperor allowed it.

sentences.zh: 因叩首謝曰：「臣今雖不居是職，然御史臺天子耳目，常行事務，可以呈省。

translations.literal: Bowing, he thanked him and said, "Though I no longer hold that post, the Censorate is the emperor's eyes and ears; routine matters may be reported to the secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed and thanked the emperor, then said, "Though I no longer hold that office, the Censorate is the emperor's eyes and ears. Ordinary business may still be reported to the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 至若監察御史奏疏、西南兩台諮禀，事關軍國，利及生民，宜令便宜聞奏，以廣視聽，不應一一拘律，遂成文具。

translations.literal: But censors' memorials and Southwest Branch Censorate reports touching military affairs and people's welfare should be relayed directly as expedient, broadening vision and hearing—not bound rigidly by law till they become empty forms.
translations.idiomatic: But memorials from supervising censors and reports from the Southwest Branch Censorate that touch on military affairs or the people's welfare should be allowed to reach the throne directly, so the emperor's vision and hearing are broadened. They should not be throttled by legal formalities until they become empty paperwork.

sentences.zh: 臣請詔台臣言事，各許實封，幸甚。」

translations.literal: Your subject requests an edict allowing censorate officials to submit sealed memorials—that would be greatly fortunate."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that censorate officials be permitted to submit sealed memorials directly to the throne. That would be a great blessing."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「憲臣以繩愆糾繆為職，苟不自檢，於擊搏何有！

translations.literal: He added, "Censorial officials exist to correct errors—if they do not examine themselves, what power have they to strike others!
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Censors exist to correct wrongdoing. If they do not hold themselves to account, what right have they to punish others?

sentences.zh: 其有貪婪敗度之人，宜付法司增條科罪，以懲欺罔。」

translations.literal: Those who are greedy and exceed bounds should be handed to the judiciary with added statutes for punishment, to deter deceit."
translations.idiomatic: Those who are greedy and exceed all bounds should be handed to the judiciary under strengthened statutes, to punish fraud and deter abuse."

sentences.zh: 制曰：「可」。

translations.literal: Edict: "Approved."
translations.idiomatic: An edict replied: "Granted."

sentences.zh: 由是臺憲得實封言事。

translations.literal: Henceforth the censorate could submit sealed memorials.
translations.idiomatic: From then on censorate officials were permitted to submit sealed memorials directly to the throne.

sentences.zh: 會尚書省立，授李資善大夫、尚書左丞，李復固辭，以謂「論臣資格，未宜遽至此」。

translations.literal: When the Ministry of Revenue was established, Ye Li was appointed Grand Master for Guidance and Left Vice Minister; he again declined, saying, "Judging by your subject's qualifications, he should not so hastily reach this rank."
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of Revenue was established, Ye Li was appointed Grand Master for Guidance and Left Vice Minister of Revenue, but he declined again, saying his qualifications did not yet warrant such rapid promotion.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「商起伊尹，周舉太公，豈循格耶！

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Shang raised up Yi Yin, Zhou elevated Taigong—would they have followed formal rank and seniority!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "The Shang rose through Yi Yin, and the Zhou through Taigong—did they wait on formal qualifications?

sentences.zh: 尚書系天下輕重，朕以煩卿，卿其勿辭。」

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue holds the weight of the realm; I burden you with it—do not decline."
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue holds the fate of the empire in its hands. I am asking this of you—please do not refuse."

sentences.zh: 賜大小車各一，許乘小車入禁中，仍給扶升殿。

translations.literal: He was granted one large carriage and one small carriage, permitted to enter the inner palace in the small carriage, and also given supports for ascending the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Li was granted one large carriage and one small carriage, permitted to ride the smaller one into the inner palace, and given walking aids to help him up the steps of the audience hall.

sentences.zh: 始定至元鈔法。

translations.literal: He first established the Zhiyuan paper currency system.
translations.idiomatic: He helped establish the Zhiyuan paper currency system.

sentences.zh: 又請立太學。

translations.literal: He also requested the founding of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned to establish the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 一日，從至柳林，奏曰：「善政不可以徒行，人才不可以驟進，必訓以德義，摩以《詩》《書》，使知古聖賢行事方略，然後賢良輩出，膏澤下流。

translations.literal: One day, accompanying the emperor to Liulin, he memorialized, "Good government cannot be carried out in vain; talent cannot be rushed forward. One must instruct with virtue and righteousness and polish with the Book of Songs and the Book of Documents, so that men know the methods and strategies of the ancient sages—then the worthy will emerge in succession and benefits will flow downward.
translations.idiomatic: One day, while accompanying the emperor to Liulin, he memorialized: "Good government cannot be imposed by decree alone, and worthy men cannot be promoted overnight. They must be trained in virtue and righteousness and steeped in the classics, so that they learn how the ancient sages governed. Only then will talent emerge in abundance and the blessings of rule reach the people below.

sentences.zh: 唐、虞、三代，咸有冑學，漢、唐明主，數幸辟雍，匪為觀美也。」

translations.literal: Tang, Yu, and the Three Dynasties all had heir-apparent schools; wise rulers of Han and Tang often visited the Imperial College—it was not merely for show."
translations.idiomatic: The Tang, Yu, and Three Dynasties all maintained schools for the crown prince's education, and wise Han and Tang emperors often visited the Imperial College—not for display, but because education was essential to good rule."

sentences.zh: 乃薦周砥等十人為祭酒等官，凡廟學規制，條具以聞，帝皆從之。

translations.literal: He then recommended Zhou Di and nine others as Chancellor and other officials; all regulations for the temple school he set forth item by item in a memorial, and the emperor approved all.
translations.idiomatic: He then recommended Zhou Di and nine others for posts including Chancellor of the Academy, and submitted a detailed plan for the school's organization. The emperor approved every proposal.

sentences.zh: 時帝欲徙江南宋宗室及大姓於北方，李乘間言：「宋已歸命，其民安於田裡。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor wished to relocate Song imperial clansmen and great families of Jiangnan to the north; Ye Li seized an opportune moment and said, "Song has already submitted; its people are settled in their fields and hamlets.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor proposed resettling Song imperial clansmen and prominent Jiangnan families in the north, Ye Li took a suitable moment to speak: "The Song have already submitted, and their people are content in their villages.

sentences.zh: 今無故聞徙，必將疑懼，萬一有奸人乘釁而起，非國之利也。」

translations.literal: Now if they hear of relocation without cause, they will surely grow suspicious and fearful; should any villain seize the opening to rise up, it would not benefit the state."
translations.idiomatic: If they suddenly hear of a mass relocation for no reason, fear and suspicion will spread. Should any troublemaker seize the opportunity to rebel, the state will suffer for it."

sentences.zh: 帝大悟，事遂寢。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly understood, and the matter was then shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw the force of the argument, and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 升尚書右丞，轉資德大夫。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue and transferred to Grand Master for Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue and given the rank of Grand Master for Virtue.

sentences.zh: 時淮、浙饑饉，穀價騰踴，李奏免江淮租稅之半，運湖廣、江西糧十七萬石至鎮江，以賑饑民。

translations.literal: At the time Huai and Zhe suffered famine and grain prices soared; Ye Li memorialized to remit half the Jianghuai land tax and transport one hundred seventy thousand shi of grain from Huguang and Jiangxi to Zhenjiang to relieve the starving people.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck Huai and Zhe and grain prices soared, Ye Li petitioned to halve Jianghuai land taxes and ship one hundred seventy thousand shi of grain from Huguang and Jiangxi to Zhenjiang to feed the hungry.

sentences.zh: 帝欲伐交趾，召李入議，李曰：「遐方遠夷，得之無益，軍旅一興，費縻巨萬，今山路險巇，深入敵境，萬一蹉跌，非所以威示遠人也。」

translations.literal: The emperor wished to attack Jiaozhi and summoned Ye Li to discuss it; Ye Li said, "A distant land and far-off barbarians—gaining them would be of no benefit. Once armies are raised, costs tie up tens of thousands. Now the mountain roads are steep and treacherous; penetrating deep into enemy territory, should we stumble even once, that is not how to display authority to distant peoples."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor proposed invading Jiaozhi, Ye Li was summoned to counsel him. Ye Li said: "It is a distant frontier land of barbarians—conquest would bring no real gain. Once war begins, costs run into the tens of thousands. The mountain roads are steep and treacherous, and a deep thrust into enemy territory risks a single misstep that would destroy our authority among distant peoples rather than enhance it."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: The plan was then halted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，昇平章政事，李固辭，許之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was promoted to Grand Councillor; Ye Li firmly declined and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was promoted to Grand Councillor, but Ye Li firmly declined and the emperor allowed it.

sentences.zh: 賜以玉帶，視秩一品，及平江田四千畝。

translations.literal: He was granted a jade belt, treated at first rank, and given four thousand mu of land in Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a jade belt, accorded first-rank status, and given four thousand mu of land in Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 於是桑哥為尚書丞相，顓擅國政，急於財利，毒及生民，事具《桑哥傳》。

translations.literal: Thereupon Sangge served as Chancellor of the Ministry of Revenue, monopolizing state affairs, urgent for profit, with poison reaching the living people—the matter is fully set forth in the Biography of Sangge.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Sangge served as Chancellor of the Ministry of Revenue, monopolizing government and obsessed with profit to the people's ruin. The full account appears in his biography.

sentences.zh: 李雖與之同事，然莫能有所匡正。

translations.literal: Although Ye Li served with him in the same office, he could do nothing to correct matters.
translations.idiomatic: Although Ye Li served alongside him, he was unable to check Sangge's abuses.

sentences.zh: 會桑哥敗，事頗連及同列。

translations.literal: When Sangge fell, the affair rather implicated his colleagues as well.
translations.idiomatic: When Sangge fell, his colleagues were implicated as well.

sentences.zh: 久之，李獨以疾得請南還。

translations.literal: After a long while, Ye Li alone, on grounds of illness, obtained permission to return south.
translations.idiomatic: In time Ye Li alone was granted leave to return south on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 揚州儒學正李淦上書言：「葉李本一黥徒，受皇帝簡知，可為千載一遇。

translations.literal: Li Gan, Director of Confucian Studies in Yangzhou, submitted a memorial saying, "Ye Li was originally a branded convict, yet the emperor singled him out for recognition—a chance of a thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Li Gan, Director of Confucian Studies in Yangzhou, submitted a memorial: "Ye Li was once a branded convict whom the emperor singled out for high office—a once-in-a-millennium opportunity.

sentences.zh: 而才近天光，即以舉桑哥為第一事；

translations.literal: Yet as soon as he came near the imperial radiance, his first act was to recommend Sangge;
translations.idiomatic: Yet scarcely had he reached court when his first act was to recommend Sangge;

sentences.zh: 禁近侍言事，以非罪殺參政郭佑、楊居寬；

translations.literal: he forbade close attendants to speak on affairs, and on false charges killed Vice Directors Guo You and Yang Jukuan;
translations.idiomatic: he forbade close attendants from speaking on state affairs, and had Vice Directors Guo You and Yang Jukuan executed on trumped-up charges;

sentences.zh: 迫御史中丞劉宣自裁，錮治書侍御史陳天祥，罷御史大夫門答佔、侍御史程文海，杖監察御史；

translations.literal: he drove Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Xuan to take his own life, imprisoned Investigating Censor Chen Tianxiang, dismissed Censor-in-Chief Mendazhan and Attending Censor Cheng Wenhui, and beat supervising censors with rods;
translations.idiomatic: he drove Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Xuan to suicide, imprisoned Investigating Censor Chen Tianxiang, dismissed Censor-in-Chief Mendazhan and Attending Censor Cheng Wenhui, and had supervising censors beaten;

sentences.zh: 變鈔法，拘學糧，征軍官俸，減兵士糧；

translations.literal: he changed the paper currency law, constrained student grain rations, levied military officers' salaries, and reduced soldiers' rations;
translations.idiomatic: he altered the paper currency system, cut student grain allowances, requisitioned military officers' salaries, and reduced soldiers' rations;

sentences.zh: 立行司農司、木綿提舉司，增鹽酒醋稅課，官民皆受其禍。

translations.literal: he established branch offices of the Ministry of Agriculture and the Cotton Monopoly Commission, increased levies on salt, wine, and vinegar, and officials and commoners alike suffered the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: he created branch agricultural offices and cotton monopoly commissions, raised taxes on salt, wine, and vinegar, and officials and commoners alike suffered for it.

sentences.zh: 尤可痛者，要束木禍湖廣，沙不丁禍江淮，滅貴裡禍福建。

translations.literal: Most painful of all, Yao Shumu brought calamity to Huguang, Shabuding to Jianghuai, and Mie Guili to Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Worst of all, Yao Shumu ravaged Huguang, Shabuding ravaged Jianghuai, and Mie Guili ravaged Fujian.

sentences.zh: 又大鉤考錢糧，民怨而盜發，天怒而地震，水災洊至。

translations.literal: Moreover there were great audits of finances and grain; the people resented and bandits arose, Heaven was angered and earthquakes occurred, and floods came in succession.
translations.idiomatic: There were sweeping audits of finances and grain. The people seethed and bandits rose; Heaven showed its anger in earthquakes, and floods followed one after another.

sentences.zh: 尚賴皇帝聖明，更張政化。

translations.literal: We still rely on the emperor's sagely clarity to reform and renew governance.
translations.idiomatic: Only the emperor's wisdom has allowed the government to be reformed.

sentences.zh: 人皆知桑哥用群小之罪，而不知葉李舉桑哥之罪。

translations.literal: All know Sangge's crime in employing petty men, but do not know Ye Li's crime in recommending Sangge.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone knows the crime of Sangge's employment of petty men, but not the crime of Ye Li's recommendation of Sangge.

sentences.zh: 葉李雖罷相權，刑戮未加，天下往往竊議，宜斬葉李以謝天下。」

translations.literal: Although Ye Li has been stripped of ministerial power, punishment has not been applied; throughout the realm people often whisper in private—it is fitting to execute Ye Li to answer to the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Ye Li has lost his ministerial power but has not been punished, and people throughout the realm murmur against him. He should be executed to satisfy public outrage."

sentences.zh: 書聞，帝矍然曰：「葉李廉介剛直，朕所素知者，寧有是耶！」

translations.literal: When the memorial was received, the emperor started and said, "Ye Li is incorruptible, upright, and firm—what I have long known of him—could this really be so!"
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, the emperor started and said, "Ye Li is honest, upright, and uncompromising—that is what I have always known of him. How could this be true?"

sentences.zh: 有旨驛召淦詣京師。

translations.literal: An order was issued to summon Gan by post relay to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial order summoned Li Gan to the capital by post relay.

sentences.zh: 二十九年二月，李南還，至臨清，帝遣使召之，俾為平章政事，佐丞相完澤治省事，李上表力辭。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twenty-ninth year, Ye Li returned south and reached Linqing; the emperor sent an envoy to summon him, appointing him Grand Councillor to assist Chancellor Wanze in managing secretariat affairs; Ye Li submitted a memorial forcefully declining.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twenty-ninth year, as Ye Li was returning south and reached Linqing, the emperor sent an envoy to summon him and appoint him Grand Councillor to assist Chancellor Wanze in running the Secretariat. Ye Li submitted a memorial firmly declining.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒，年五十一。

translations.literal: Before long he died, aged fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died, at the age of fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 李既卒而淦至，詔以淦為江陰路教授，以旌直言。

translations.literal: After Ye Li had died Gan arrived; an edict appointed Gan Instructor of the Jiangyin Circuit to honor forthright speech.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Li had already died when Li Gan arrived. The emperor appointed Gan Instructor of the Jiangyin Circuit to honor his candor.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問兵部郎中趙孟頫，李與留夢炎孰優，孟頫對：「夢炎優。」

translations.literal: The emperor once asked Zhao Mengfu, Director in the Ministry of War, whether Ye Li or Liu Mengyan was superior; Mengfu answered, "Mengyan is superior."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once asked Zhao Mengfu of the Ministry of War whether Ye Li or Liu Mengyan was the better man. Mengfu replied, "Mengyan is superior."

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「不然，夢炎以掄魁位宰相，而附賈似道，病民誤國，伴食中書，無所可否；

translations.literal: The emperor smiled and said, "Not so. Mengyan, as top examination graduate, held the post of chief minister yet attached himself to Jia Sidao, harming the people and misleading the state—an idler at the Secretariat who neither approved nor disapproved;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor smiled and said, "Not so. Mengyan topped the examinations and became chief minister, yet he attached himself to Jia Sidao, harmed the people, and misled the state—a useless ornament in the Secretariat who never took a stand on anything.

sentences.zh: 李舊由諸生，力詆似道，其過夢炎甚遠。

translations.literal: Ye Li came from the ranks of students and vigorously denounced Sidao—his superiority over Mengyan is very far.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Li came from the common scholar class and fiercely denounced Jia Sidao. In that respect he far surpassed Mengyan.

sentences.zh: 然其性剛直，人不能容，而朕獨愛之也。」

translations.literal: Yet his nature is firm and straight, and others cannot tolerate him—but I alone cherish him.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was uncompromising, and others found him hard to bear—but I alone valued him for it.

sentences.zh: 李前後被賜之物甚多，而自奉甚儉。

translations.literal: Ye Li received many gifts from the emperor before and after, yet maintained himself very frugally.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had showered Ye Li with gifts over the years, yet Ye Li lived very modestly.

sentences.zh: 嘗戒其子曰：「吾世業儒，甘貧約，唯以忠義結主知。

translations.literal: He once admonished his sons, saying, "Our family for generations has practiced Confucian learning, content with poverty and restraint, winning the ruler's recognition only through loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He once warned his sons: "Our family has been scholars for generations, content with poverty and simplicity. We have won the emperor's trust only through loyalty and integrity.

sentences.zh: 汝曹其清慎自持，勿增吾過。」

translations.literal: You must maintain yourselves with integrity and caution—do not add to my faults."
translations.idiomatic: You must hold yourselves to integrity and caution. Do not add to my faults."

sentences.zh: 指所賜物曰：「此終當還官也。」

translations.literal: Pointing to the gifts he had received, he said, "These in the end must be returned to the state."
translations.idiomatic: Pointing to the gifts he had received, he said, "These must all be returned to the state in the end."

sentences.zh: 比卒，悉表送官，一毫不以自私。

translations.literal: When he died, he memorialized and sent them all to the state, not keeping a single item for himself.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his family memorialized and sent every gift back to the state. He had kept nothing for himself.

sentences.zh: 至正八年，贈資德大夫、江浙等處行中書省右丞、上護軍，追封南陽郡公，諡文簡。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhizheng he was posthumously granted Grand Master for Virtue, Right Vice Director of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, and Senior Guardian of the State, enfeoffed as Duke of Nanyang Commandery, with posthumous title Wen Jian.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Zhizheng he was posthumously granted the ranks of Grand Master for Virtue, Right Vice Director of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, and Senior Guardian of the State, enfeoffed posthumously as Duke of Nanyang Commandery, with the posthumous title Wen Jian.

sentences.zh: ○燕公楠

translations.literal: ○ Yan Gongnan
translations.idiomatic: Biography: Yan Gongnan

sentences.zh: 燕公楠，字國材，南康之建昌人，宋禮部侍郎肅之七世孫。

translations.literal: Yan Gongnan, style name Guocai, was a man of Jianchang in Nankang, seventh-generation descendant of Su, Vice Minister of Rites of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Gongnan, whose courtesy name was Guocai, came from Jianchang in Nankang Prefecture. He was the seventh-generation descendant of Su, Vice Minister of Rites under the Song.

sentences.zh: 母雷氏，夢五色巨翼入幃，遂生公楠。

translations.literal: His mother was the Lady Lei; she dreamed that five-colored giant wings entered the bed curtains, and thereafter Gongnan was born.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Lei, dreamed that giant wings of five colors entered her bed curtains, and soon after Yan Gongnan was born.

sentences.zh: 十歲能屬文，居父喪，廬墓三年。

translations.literal: At ten he could compose prose; during his father's mourning he dwelt by the tomb for three years.
translations.idiomatic: At ten he could already compose essays. When his father died, he mourned at the grave for three years.

sentences.zh: 再貢於鄉，不第，後以連帥辟，五遷至通判贛州事。

translations.literal: Twice he presented himself at the district examinations and did not pass; later he was recruited by the regional commander and was promoted five times to Vice Prefect of Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He failed the provincial examinations twice, but was later recruited by the regional commander and rose through five promotions to Vice Prefect of Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 至元十三年，世祖既平江南，帥臣板授同知贛州事。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhiyuan, after the Founder had pacified Jiangnan, the commander provisionally appointed him Associate Prefect of Ganzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 1276, after Kublai had pacified Jiangnan, the regional commander provisionally appointed him Associate Prefect of Ganzhou.

sentences.zh: 十四年，以平廣南功，遷同知吉州路總管府事。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, for merit in pacifying Guangnan, he was transferred to Associate Administrator of the Jizhou Circuit Chief Office.
translations.idiomatic: In 1277, for his service in pacifying Guangnan, he was transferred to Associate Administrator of the Jizhou Circuit.

sentences.zh: 二十二年夏，召至上都，奏對稱旨，世祖賜名賽因囊加帶，命參大政，辭，乞補外。

translations.literal: In the summer of the twenty-second year he was summoned to Shangdu; his memorial and answers pleased the Founder, who granted him the name Saiyin Nangjiadai, ordered him to participate in major governance, but he declined and begged for a provincial appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of 1285 he was summoned to Shangdu. His audience pleased Kublai, who granted him the Mongol name Saiyin Nangjiadai and ordered him to join the central government. He declined and asked for a provincial post instead.

sentences.zh: 除僉江浙行中書省事，俄移江淮。

translations.literal: He was appointed Associate Director of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, and soon transferred to Jianghuai.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Associate Director of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat, and soon transferred to the Jianghuai Branch.

sentences.zh: 尚書省立，就僉江淮行尚書省事。

translations.literal: When the Ministry of Revenue was established, he was appointed Associate Director of the Jianghuai Branch Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of Revenue was established, he became Associate Director of the Jianghuai Branch Ministry.

sentences.zh: 江淮在宋為邊陲，故多閒田，公楠請置兩淮屯田，勸導有方，田日以墾。

translations.literal: Jianghuai under the Song had been a frontier, so there was much idle land; Gongnan requested the establishment of garrison farming in the two Huai regions, guided and encouraged with effective methods, and fields were daily opened.
translations.idiomatic: Jianghuai had been a Song frontier, leaving much land uncultivated. Yan Gongnan proposed establishing garrison farms in the two Huai regions. His guidance was effective, and fields were brought under cultivation day by day.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，除大司農，領八道勸農營田司事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was appointed Grand Minister of Agriculture and oversaw the Encourage Agriculture and Colonization Commissions of eight circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In 1288 he was appointed Grand Minister of Agriculture and placed in charge of the Encourage Agriculture and Colonization Commissions across eight circuits.

sentences.zh: 按行郡縣，興利舉弊，績用大著。

translations.literal: Touring prefectures and counties, he promoted benefits and exposed abuses; his achievements were greatly notable.
translations.idiomatic: Touring prefectures and counties, he promoted what benefited the people and exposed abuses. His achievements were widely recognized.

sentences.zh: 劾江西營田使沙不丁貪橫，罷之。

translations.literal: He impeached Shabuding, Commissioner of Colonization Farms in Jiangxi, for greed and overbearing conduct, and had him dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached Shabuding, the Jiangxi Colonization Commissioner, for greed and abuse of power, and had him removed from office.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，拜江淮行中書省參知政事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he was appointed Vice Director of the Jianghuai Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1290 he was appointed Vice Director of the Jianghuai Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 桑哥既敗，而蠹政未盡去，民不堪命。

translations.literal: Although Sangge had fallen, corrupt policies were not fully removed, and the people could not bear the burdens.
translations.idiomatic: Although Sangge had fallen, corrupt policies remained and the people could not endure the burdens imposed on them.

sentences.zh: 公楠赴闕，極陳其故，請更張以固國本。

translations.literal: Gongnan went to court and thoroughly stated the reasons, requesting reform to solidify the foundation of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Gongnan went to court, laid out the causes at length, and petitioned for reform to strengthen the foundations of the state.

sentences.zh: 世祖悅。

translations.literal: The Founder was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai was pleased.

sentences.zh: 會欲易政府大臣，以問公楠，公楠薦伯顏、不灰木、阇裡、闊里吉思、史弼、徐琰、趙琪、陳天祥等十人。

translations.literal: When the emperor wished to change senior government ministers, he asked Gongnan, and Gongnan recommended ten men: Bayan, Buqaimu, Chali, Qochoqai, Shi Bi, Xu Yan, Zhao Qi, Chen Tianxiang, and others.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor wished to replace senior ministers, he consulted Yan Gongnan, who recommended ten men: Bayan, Buqaimu, Chali, Qochoqai, Shi Bi, Xu Yan, Zhao Qi, Chen Tianxiang, and others.

sentences.zh: 又問孰可以為首相，對曰：「天下人望所屬，莫若安童。」

translations.literal: He was again asked who could serve as chief minister, and answered, "Where the expectation of the realm rests, none surpasses Antong."
translations.idiomatic: Asked who should serve as chief minister, he replied, "The man in whom the hopes of the realm rest is Antong."

sentences.zh: 問其次，曰：「完澤可。」

translations.literal: Asked who would be next, he said, "Wanze would do."
translations.idiomatic: Asked who would be next, he said, "Wanze would serve."

sentences.zh: 明日，拜完澤為丞相，以公楠及不灰木為平章政事，固辭。

translations.literal: The next day Wanze was appointed chief minister, and Gongnan and Buqaimu were made Grand Councillors; they firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Wanze was appointed chief minister, and Yan Gongnan and Buqaimu were appointed Grand Councillors, but both firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 改江浙行中書省參知政事，賜弓矢及衛士十人以行。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Director of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat and granted bow and arrows and ten guards for his journey.
translations.idiomatic: He was instead appointed Vice Director of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat and granted a bow, arrows, and ten guards for his journey.

sentences.zh: 三十年，復為大司農，得藏匿公私田六萬九千八百六十二頃，歲出粟十五萬一千一百斛、鈔二千六百貫、帛千五百匹、麻絲二千七百斤。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he again served as Grand Minister of Agriculture and recovered sixty-nine thousand eight hundred sixty-two qing of concealed public and private fields, yielding annually one hundred fifty-one thousand one hundred shi of grain, two thousand six hundred strings of paper money, one thousand five hundred bolts of silk, and two thousand seven hundred jin of hemp and thread.
translations.idiomatic: In 1293 he again became Grand Minister of Agriculture. He recovered nearly seventy thousand qing of concealed public and private land, which yielded annually more than one hundred fifty thousand shi of grain, two thousand six hundred strings of paper money, one thousand five hundred bolts of silk, and two thousand seven hundred jin of hemp and thread.

sentences.zh: 元貞元年，進河南行省右丞，厘正鹽法，民便之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanzhen he was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Henan Branch Secretariat, rectified the salt law, and the people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: In 1295 he was promoted to Right Vice Director of the Henan Branch Secretariat, where he reformed the salt monopoly to the people's benefit.

sentences.zh: 召入覲。

translations.literal: He was summoned to audience at court.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court for an audience.

sentences.zh: 成宗以公楠先帝舊臣，慰勞良至，改拜江浙行省右丞。

translations.literal: Chengzong, because Gongnan was an old minister of the previous emperor, consoled him with utmost warmth and changed his appointment to Right Vice Director of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong received him with great warmth as a veteran of his predecessor's reign and appointed him Right Vice Director of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明年，遷湖廣行省右丞。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 轉運司判官唐申，家沅州，豪橫奪民田；

translations.literal: Tang Shen, Assistant Commissioner of the Transport Bureau, was from Yuanzhou and overbearingly seized people's fields;
translations.idiomatic: Tang Shen, an assistant commissioner of the Transport Bureau from Yuanzhou, had seized people's land by force;

sentences.zh: 武昌縣尹劉權殺主簿，誣係其妻子。

translations.literal: Liu Quan, Magistrate of Wuchang County, killed the chief clerk and falsely implicated and imprisoned his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Quan, Magistrate of Wuchang County, had murdered the chief clerk and falsely implicated the clerk's wife and children.

sentences.zh: 悉正其罪。

translations.literal: He corrected the crimes of all of them.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Gongnan saw that justice was done in both cases.

sentences.zh: 五年，召還朝，以卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was summoned back to court and there died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of his reign Chengzong summoned him back to court, where he died.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，甚傷悼之。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he grieved deeply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply grieved when he heard the news.

sentences.zh: 賻贈有加，特命朝臣護喪南歸。

translations.literal: Funeral gifts and posthumous honors were increased, and court officials were specially ordered to escort the funeral procession south.
translations.idiomatic: Funeral gifts and posthumous honors were increased, and court officials were specially ordered to escort his body home to the south.

sentences.zh: ○馬紹

translations.literal: ○ Ma Shao
translations.idiomatic: Biography: Ma Shao

sentences.zh: 馬紹，字​​子卿，濟州金鄉人，從上黨張播學。

translations.literal: Ma Shao, style name Ziqing, was a man of Jinxiang in Jizhou; he studied under Zhang Bo of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shao, whose courtesy name was Ziqing, came from Jinxiang in Jizhou. He studied under Zhang Bo of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 丞相安童入侍世祖，奏言宜得儒士講論經史，以資見聞。

translations.literal: Chancellor Antong, attending the Founder, memorialized that Confucian scholars should be obtained to discuss the classics and history, to enrich knowledge and experience.
translations.idiomatic: When Chancellor Antong attended Kublai, he proposed recruiting Confucian scholars to discuss the classics and history and broaden the emperor's learning.

sentences.zh: 平章政事張啟元以紹應詔，授左右司都事。

translations.literal: Grand Councillor Zhang Qiyuan, with Shao responding to the imperial summons, had him appointed Chief Secretary of the Left and Right Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councillor Zhang Qiyuan nominated Ma Shao in response to the imperial summons, and he was appointed Chief Secretary of the Left and Right Offices.

sentences.zh: 出知單州，民刻石頌德。

translations.literal: Sent out as Prefect of Shanzhou, the people carved stone to praise his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When he was sent out as Prefect of Shanzhou, the people erected a stone monument in his praise.

sentences.zh: 至元十年，僉山東東西道提刑按察司事。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhiyuan he was appointed Associate Commissioner of the Shandong East and West Circuit Surveillance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In 1273 he was appointed Associate Commissioner of the Shandong East and West Circuit Surveillance Commission.

sentences.zh: 益都寧海飢，紹發粟賑之。

translations.literal: Yidu and Ninghai suffered famine; Shao distributed grain to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck Yidu and Ninghai, Ma Shao distributed grain to relieve the suffering.

sentences.zh: 十三年，移僉河北河南道提刑按察司事。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to Associate Commissioner of the Hebei and Henan Circuit Surveillance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In 1276 he was transferred to Associate Commissioner of the Hebei and Henan Circuit Surveillance Commission.

sentences.zh: 未行，屬江淮甫定，選官撫治，遷同知和州路總管府事，民賴以安。

translations.literal: Before he departed, as Jianghuai had just been pacified and officials were being selected to govern and soothe the region, he was transferred to Associate Administrator of the Hezhou Circuit Chief Office, and the people relied on him for peace.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the new post, Jianghuai had just been pacified and needed officials to govern it. He was transferred to Associate Administrator of the Hezhou Circuit, where the people found security under his rule.

sentences.zh: 十九年，詔割隆興為東宮分地，皇太子選署總管，召至京師，為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year an edict partitioned Longxing as crown prince's fief; the crown prince selected and appointed him chief administrator, summoned him to the capital, and made him Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In 1282 an edict partitioned Longxing as crown prince's fief. The crown prince selected Ma Shao as chief administrator, summoned him to the capital, and appointed him Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 萬億庫吏盜絨四兩，時相欲置之重典，紹言：「物情俱輕，宜從貸減。」

translations.literal: A clerk of the Ten Thousand Heaps Treasury stole four liang of velvet; the chief minister at the time wished to impose the heavy penalty, but Shao said, "The goods are altogether light in value—it is fitting to grant leniency and reduce the punishment."
translations.idiomatic: A clerk of the Ten Thousand Heaps Treasury stole four liang of velvet. The chief minister wanted the harshest penalty, but Ma Shao argued: "The goods were of little value. The punishment should be reduced."

sentences.zh: 乃決杖釋之。

translations.literal: He then decided on beating with rods and released him.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shao ordered him beaten with rods and released.

sentences.zh: 河間李移住妄言惑眾，謀為不軌，紹被檄按問，所全活幾百人。

translations.literal: Li Yizhu of Hejian, with false talk confusing the masses, plotted rebellion; Shao was under edict to investigate and interrogate, and those he spared amounted to nearly a hundred people.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Yizhu of Hejian spread seditious rumors and was accused of plotting rebellion, Ma Shao was ordered to investigate. He spared nearly a hundred people who would otherwise have been condemned.

sentences.zh: 二十年，參議中書省事。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he deliberated Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1283 he was appointed Deliberator of Secretariat Affairs.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，改兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was changed to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In 1285 he was transferred to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 踰年，復為刑部尚書。

translations.literal: After a year he again served as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he returned to the post of Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，分立尚書省，擢拜參知政事，賜中統鈔五千緡。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year a separate Ministry of Revenue was established; he was promoted and appointed Vice Director, granted five thousand strings of Zhongtong paper money.
translations.idiomatic: In 1287, when a separate Ministry of Revenue was established, he was promoted to Vice Director and granted five thousand strings of Zhongtong paper money.

sentences.zh: 時更印至元鈔，前信州三務提舉杜

translations.literal: At the time new Zhiyuan paper notes were being issued; the former Commissioner of the Three Offices in Xinzhou, Du
translations.idiomatic: When new Zhiyuan paper notes were being issued, the former Commissioner of the Three Offices in Xinzhou, Du

sentences.zh: 璠言至元鈔公私非便。

translations.literal: Fan said that the Zhiyuan notes were inconvenient for public and private use.
translations.idiomatic: Fan argued that the Zhiyuan notes were inconvenient for both government and private use.

sentences.zh: 平章政事桑哥怒曰：「杜璠何人，敢沮吾鈔法耶！」

translations.literal: Grand Councillor Sangge said angrily, "Who is Du Fan, that he dares obstruct my paper-note policy!"
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councillor Sangge flew into a rage. "Who is Du Fan," he demanded, "to dare block my currency reform?"

sentences.zh: 欲當以重罪。

translations.literal: He wished to have him convicted of a heavy crime.
translations.idiomatic: He wanted Fan punished with the harshest penalty.

sentences.zh: 紹從容言曰：「國家導人使言，言可採，用之；

translations.literal: Shao said calmly, "The state guides people to speak; if what is said can be adopted, employ it;
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shao replied calmly, "The throne encourages people to speak out. When counsel is sound, it should be taken up;

sentences.zh: 不可採，亦不之罪。

translations.literal: if it cannot be adopted, neither punish him.
translations.idiomatic: when it is not, the speaker should go unpunished.

sentences.zh: 今重罪之，豈不與詔書違戾乎？」

translations.literal: Now to punish him heavily—would that not conflict with the edict?"
translations.idiomatic: To punish him severely now would fly in the face of the emperor's own edict, would it not?"

sentences.zh: 璠得免。

translations.literal: Fan was thereby spared.
translations.idiomatic: Fan was spared.

sentences.zh: 拜尚書左丞。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shao was appointed Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 親王戍邊，其士卒有過支廩米者，有司以聞，帝欲究問加罪。

translations.literal: Imperial princes were garrisoning the frontier; some of their soldiers had overdrawn their granary rations. The responsible officials reported it, and the emperor wished to investigate and punish them.
translations.idiomatic: While imperial princes held frontier garrisons, some of their troops drew more than their allotted grain rations. When officials reported this, the emperor wanted a full inquiry and punishment.

sentences.zh: 紹言：「方邊庭用兵，罪之，懼失將士心。

translations.literal: Shao said, "Just as the frontier is at war, to punish them would fear losing the hearts of officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shao argued, "The frontier is at war. Punishing them now would only alienate officers and men.

sentences.zh: 所支逾數者，當嗣年之數可也。」

translations.literal: For those who drew more than their allotment, let them make up the amount in succeeding years—that will suffice."
translations.idiomatic: Let those who took too much repay it from future allotments—that should be enough."

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: The edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 宗親海都作亂，其民來歸者七十餘萬，散居雲、朔間。

translations.literal: The imperial clansman Haidu rebelled; more than seven hundred thousand of his people came over and submitted, scattered living between Yun and Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial clansman Haidu rebelled, more than seven hundred thousand of his followers defected and were scattered across the Yun and Shuo region.

sentences.zh: 桑哥議徙之內地就食，紹持不可。

translations.literal: Sangge proposed moving them inland to find food; Shao maintained that this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Sangge proposed resettling them inland where they could be fed, but Ma Shao objected.

sentences.zh: 桑哥怒曰：「馬左丞愛惜漢人，欲令餒死此輩耶？」

translations.literal: Sangge said angrily, "Vice Director Ma cherishes the Han Chinese—does he wish to let these people starve to death?"
translations.idiomatic: Sangge raged, "Vice Director Ma coddles the Han—does he mean to let these people starve?"

sentences.zh: 紹徐曰：「南土地燠，北人居之，慮生疾疫。

translations.literal: Shao said slowly, "The southern lands are warm; if northerners dwell there, one fears pestilence will arise.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shao answered evenly, "The south is hot and humid. If northerners settle there, plague is likely to break out.

sentences.zh: 若恐餒死，葛若計口給羊馬之資，俾還本土，則未歸者孰不欣慕。

translations.literal: If you fear they will starve, why not allocate per capita provisions of sheep and horses and have them return to their homeland—then who among those who have not yet submitted would not joyfully look to do the same?
translations.idiomatic: If the fear is starvation, why not give each person sheep and horses enough to live on and send them home? Who among those still on Haidu's side would not gladly follow?

sentences.zh: 言有異同，丞相何以怒為？

translations.literal: When speech differs, why should the chief minister grow angry?
translations.idiomatic: When views differ, why should the chief minister take offense?

sentences.zh: 宜取聖裁。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to seek the sage's decision."
translations.idiomatic: Let the emperor decide."

sentences.zh: 乃如紹言以聞，帝曰：「馬秀才所言是也。」

translations.literal: Thereupon they reported as Shao had said; the emperor said, "What Ma the scholar said is correct."
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was reported to the throne as Ma Shao had urged. The emperor said, "Ma the scholar is right."

sentences.zh: 桑哥集諸路總管三十人，導之入見，欲以趣辦財賦之多寡為殿最。

translations.literal: Sangge gathered thirty circuit chiefs, led them in for audience, and wished to use the amount of revenue hurriedly collected as the standard for ranking them.
translations.idiomatic: Sangge assembled thirty circuit administrators, brought them before the emperor, and proposed ranking them by how quickly each had squeezed out revenue.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「財賦辦集，非民力困竭必不能。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "For revenues to be fully collected, unless the people's strength is exhausted it surely cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "Full revenue collection is impossible unless the people are driven to exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 然朕之府軍，豈少此哉！」

translations.literal: Yet is my treasury and army so lacking in this!"
translations.idiomatic: Yet my treasury and armies are hardly so desperate for it!"

sentences.zh: 紹退至省，追錄聖訓，付太史書之。

translations.literal: Shao withdrew to the ministry, wrote down the sacred instruction from memory, and entrusted it to the Grand Historian to record.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shao withdrew to the ministry, transcribed the emperor's words from memory, and had them entered in the official annals by the Grand Historian.

sentences.zh: 議增鹽課，紹獨力爭山東課不可增。

translations.literal: When salt levies were discussed for increase, Shao alone strenuously argued that Shandong's levy must not be raised.
translations.idiomatic: When a salt-tax increase was proposed, Ma Shao alone fought to keep the Shandong rate from going up.

sentences.zh: 議增賦，紹曰：「苟不節浮費，雖重斂數倍，亦不足也。」

translations.literal: When tax increases were discussed, Shao said, "If wasteful spending is not curbed, even if levies were doubled several times, it would still not suffice."
translations.idiomatic: When general tax hikes came up, Ma Shao said, "Unless extravagant spending is cut, doubling the levies would still not be enough."

sentences.zh: 事遂寢。

translations.literal: The matter was then dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Both proposals were shelved.

sentences.zh: 都城種苜蓿地，分給居民，權勢因取為己有，以一區授紹，紹獨不取。

translations.literal: Alfalfa-growing land in the capital was apportioned to residents; the powerful seized it for themselves. One plot was granted to Shao, but Shao alone did not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Alfalfa fields in the capital had been parceled out to residents, but the powerful seized the plots for themselves. One parcel was offered to Ma Shao; he alone refused it.

sentences.zh: 桑哥欲奏請賜紹，紹辭曰：「紹以非才居政府，恆憂不能塞責，詎敢徼非分之福，以速罪戾！」

translations.literal: Sangge wished to memorialize requesting that it be granted to Shao; Shao declined, saying, "Shao, with inadequate talent occupying a government post, constantly fears being unable to fulfill his duty—how dare he seek undeserved good fortune and hasten guilt and punishment!"
translations.idiomatic: Sangge wanted to petition the throne to grant him the land anyway. Ma Shao refused: "I hold office beyond my merits and already fear I cannot meet my obligations. How dare I grasp at unearned favor and invite disaster?"

sentences.zh: 桑哥敗，跡其所嘗行賂者，索其籍閱之，獨無紹名。

translations.literal: When Sangge fell, they traced those to whom he had given bribes, sought his registers and reviewed them—Shao's name alone was not there.
translations.idiomatic: After Sangge's downfall, investigators traced everyone he had bribed and examined his ledgers. Ma Shao's name was nowhere among them.

sentences.zh: 桑哥既敗，乃曰：「使吾早信馬左丞之言，必不至今日之禍。」

translations.literal: After Sangge had fallen, he then said, "Had I early believed Vice Director Ma's words, I would certainly not have come to today's disaster."
translations.idiomatic: When Sangge was ruined, he said, "Had I listened to Vice Director Ma sooner, I would never have come to this ruin."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「馬左丞忠潔可尚，其復舊職。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Vice Director Ma's loyalty and integrity are to be honored; let him resume his former post."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Vice Director Ma's loyalty and integrity deserve praise. Restore him to his former post."

sentences.zh: 尚書省罷，改中書左丞，居再歲，移疾還家。

translations.literal: When the Ministry of Revenue was abolished, he was changed to Left Vice Director of the Central Secretariat; after two years he cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of Revenue was abolished, he became Left Vice Director of the Central Secretariat. After two years he pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 元貞元年，遷中書右丞，行江浙省事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanzhen he was transferred to Right Vice Director of the Central Secretariat and served concurrently as acting chief of the Jiang-Zhe Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1295 he was made Right Vice Director of the Central Secretariat and acting chief of the Jiang-Zhe branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 大德三年，移河南省。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dade he was transferred to Henan Province.
translations.idiomatic: In 1299 he was transferred to Henan Province.

sentences.zh: 明年卒。

translations.literal: The next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following year.

sentences.zh: 有詩文數百篇。

translations.literal: He left several hundred poems and essays.
translations.idiomatic: He left several hundred poems and prose pieces.
